events.description:
We need to rethink how power operates in the age of AI. Social theorist Steven Lukes’ now classic text Power: A Radical View sees the operation of power in three dimensions — as prevailing in observable conflicts, as preempting these by controlling agendas and, least observably, as shaping thought, desires, and beliefs. AI seems to be transforming these ways of securing the compliance of others, taking them beyond human agency altogether. Steven Lukes will return alongside philosopher Audrey Borowski to discuss these troubling questions on the occasion of a new issue of his famous analysis.

“Steven Lukes stirred up an intellectual firestorm.” – Michael Walzer

A Forum for European Philosophy event
events.title: Power in the Age of AI

events.description: Robert Rauschenberg broke boundaries between high art and popular culture, radically transforming Abstract Art. Explore the lasting legacy of this pioneering artist's work across painting, sculpture and performance.
events.title: Robert Rauschenberg: Everything is Art

events.description:
From Peter Thiel’s doctrine of the “sovereign individual” to Drake’s call to “know yourself, know your worth,” self-knowledge is seen as the clear winner of our modern age. Therapists and a multi-billion dollar self-help industry promise to reveal and improve our inner selves, while modern neuroscience claims to decode the self into the firing of neurons. But critics argue the self is elusive and fundamentally unknowable. A self that tries to know itself is like an eye that tries to see itself. Schopenhauer, echoing ancient Indian thought, called the self “that which knows all things and is known by none,” while Wittgenstein argued that the self is not part of the world at all, but is rather its limit.

Should we give up on the idea that the self can be known like any other object? Does this unknowable self mean that the world that science investigates is necessarily incomplete? Or can the self be demystified, dragged into the light and studied like anything else?

Pioneering philosopher of panpsychism Galen Strawson, post-postmodern philosopher Hilary Lawson, and rising star philosopher Victoria Trumbull debate knowing the self.

In partnership with Philosophy Now
events.speakers: Galen Strawson, Hilary Lawson, Victoria Trumbull. Jack Symes hosts
events.title: The Self and Its Shadows

events.description:
Many see young people as the losers of modern capitalism. House prices have skyrocketed, wages stagnated, and debt is way up. On average, millennials at 35 have nearly a third less wealth than boomers did at the same age. But the story is not straightforward. We’re in the early stages of the largest wealth transfer in history, with $84 trillion expected to be passed on in the US by 2045. This inheritance won’t be handed out evenly. Some will become wealthy through no effort of their own, while others without rich parents will have a radically different lifestyle. Critics argue the real disparity is not between the generations but between those who will inherit and those who won't.

Should we focus less on the generational divide and instead focus on how to make the inequality of inheritance less severe? Or by addressing the challenges of younger generations can we reduce the impact of inheritance? Then again, if the underlying problem is housing costs, could we get rid of planning and zoning and thereby reduce prices for the young and cut the wealth of older generations?

World-leading economist Mariana Mazzucato, former Chancellor Kwasi Kwarteng, and Green Party Deputy Leader Rachel Millward debate inheritance and inequality.
events.speakers: Rachel Millward, Kwasi Kwarteng, Mariana Mazzucato. Philip Collins hosts
events.title: The $84 Trillion Lottery

events.description: If you sit on a table, does it magically become a chair? What about if you sit on a dog, or some slime — are they now chairs? At least we know that a chair is a chair... or is it? Join The Philosophy Foundation's Jo Haire to hear a fantastical story exploring how objects, their meaning, and purpose are all up for some serious questioning
events.title: What Is A Chair?

events.description:
The novel was once at the centre of cultural life — providing the highpoints and showcase of genius, a demanding art that asked readers to sit alone with difficulty. But the readers are disappearing. Fewer than half of American adults now read a single book in a year, and only 38% read any fiction at all. Join Booker-shortlisted author of Umbrella, Will Self, as he argues this is nothing short of a civilisational crisis. The challenging novel has been pushed to the margins by digital media and "synthetic fluff", and we risk losing our capacity for depth of thought altogether. In conversation with novelist and essayist Joanna Kavenna, they ask whether the book is in terminal decline, and whether anything can be done about it.

"Unsettling and furiously intelligent." – Guardian

"Endlessly inventive." – The Times
events.title: The End of the Book: A Civilisation in Crisis

events.description:
Tipped as the "next Albert Einstein", Sabrina Pasterski isn't undertaking her cutting-edge research in theoretical physics alone. Join Pasterski as she reveals how she is attempting to automate theoretical physics research using AI and robotics. Specializing in celestial holography - an attempt to solve the problem of quantum gravity by describing our four-dimensional universe as a lower dimensional hologram living on the night sky - Pasterski explores the possibilities for her research at the frontier of AI physics.

"Her potential is off the charts." – Allen Haggerty, MIT
events.title: The Holographic Universe and The Rise of AI Physics

events.description:
Liven up your afternoon with a glass of champagne, cake, and conversation with some of the world's leading thinkers.

Neuroscience has been looking for consciousness in all the wrong places. The man who discovered the brain mechanisms of dreaming, Mark Solms, author of The Hidden Spring, has spent his career overturning what we thought we knew about the mind. Join him to discover his answer to the hard problem of consciousness.

events.description: Follow three firefighters recovering from PTSD through an innovative programme combining group therapy and ketamine. Featuring leading trauma expert Bessel van der Kolk, author of the bestselling The Body Keeps the Score.
events.title: Quiet the Sirens: Ketamine Treatments for Trauma

events.description:
What if the Big Bang isn't a singularity at the beginning of time, but a mirror in which another universe is reflected? Join Higgs Chair of Theoretical Physics, Neil Turok, as he argues our universe has a twin running backwards in time on the other side of the Big Bang, one in which antiparticles outnumber particles. This single idea, he contends, resolves dark matter and dark energy, explains why matter exists at all, and does away with the problem of inflation entirely.

"An architect of modern cosmology." – Brian Greene
events.title: The Big Bang Hides A Mirror Universe

events.description:
From the health service to the army, waste disposal to public transport, we see our public institutions as serving the people and being there for the benefit of all. But Pournelle's Iron Law of Bureaucracy proposes that in any social organisation, those that serve the original mission lose out to those who work for the preservation and expansion of the system itself. From Soviet bureaucracy to federal agencies and 'Yes Minister' thinking — strengthening the organisation and hierarchy — wins out. Foucault broadened the case, arguing that all institutions, including seemingly well-meaning professional groups like doctors and nurses, teachers and charities, are vehicles for power, and their primary function is to maintain and strengthen the organisation itself. Harvard University, for example, has three times as many administrators as teaching staff — more even in fact than undergraduates.

Are all organisations and bodies sources of, and vehicles for, power? Should we be equally sceptical of all institutions, whether charities or professional bodies, banks or corporate giants? Or is this a travesty of human endeavour, which is capable of selfless motivation and vision and should be praised as such?

Heterodox sociologist Frank Furedi, Labour life peer Thangam Debbonaire, and left-wing critic of the progressive elite Catherine Liu debate whether institutions serve only themselves.
events.speakers: Frank Furedi, Thangam Debbonaire, Catherine Liu. Roger Hearing hosts
events.title: The Monster in the Machine

events.description:
Today it is commonplace to describe our outlook as "my truth", "my lived experience". As if to recognise the radically subjective character of all outlooks. Yet at the same time, the majority also wish to hold onto some aspects of reality that are seen as unchallengeable. Core political beliefs, about injustice or oppression, are held not to be perspectives but undeniable insights. Critics argue this partial perspectivalism is incoherent and self-serving. They argue different cultures and different individuals do not hold different perspectives on a single reality, but live in different realities. One culture's freedom fighter is another culture's terrorist. The same is true in science. As Thomas Kuhn demonstrated, a new paradigm does not simply apply a new theory, but alters what are identified as the facts.

Should we conclude that we don't share a reality but instead operate in different realities? Can we never make contact with reality as it truly is? Or must it be the case that we can gain insight into how things ultimately are, even if only from a particular point of view?

Founder of Wikipedia Jimmy Wales, post-truth philosopher Steve Fuller, and pioneer of feminist social theory Sally Haslanger debate whether we all live in different realities.
events.speakers: Steve Fuller, Jimmy Wales, Sally Haslanger. Philip Collins hosts
events.title: Reality in the Age of Perspective

events.description:
Why do people pour their lives into art no one will see, or turn to violence just to feel significant? Join philosopher and novelist Rebecca Goldstein — a MacArthur "Genius" Fellow who has spent her career probing what gives life meaning — in conversation with David Edmonds, as she argues both impulses spring from a deep, biologically rooted longing to matter. This hunger drives our greatest achievements and ugliest conflicts alike, and we must learn to satisfy it without turning against each other.

"Rebecca Goldstein helps us to see that so much of our lives, and human history, is driven by the need to matter." – Jonathan Haidt
events.title: The Dangerous Need To Matter

events.description:
Every generation inherits advice from the last about how to succeed in life. Study hard. Master your field. Build expertise. Daniel Susskind argues that most of this is now dangerously out of date. Economist, Senior Research Associate at Oxford's Institute for Ethics in AI, and a TED Talk on the future of work watched by millions, Susskind argues we have been preparing children for a world that no longer exists. Join him for his vision of what the future of education and career will look like — rebuilt from scratch for the humans who will share the world with intelligent machines.

"Wise and brilliant." – Mustafa Suleyman
events.title: Rethinking Education in the Age of AI

events.description: In the Pacific Islands — where communities have relied on the sea for generations — a new tide is coming. Plastic waste is washing ashore on the world's most remote coastlines. Chiefs, elders and community leaders share their fight for solutions.

"Maia is a natural. Born to do it. Unreal!" – Shaparak Khorsandi

events.description:
Countries have been the focus of power for over a century. Named by Le Monde as one of 70 people making the world of tomorrow, join novelist and essayist Rana Dasgupta as he argues American hegemony, Western debt, and the rise of tech firms as geopolitical actors have shattered a system many thought eternal. Looking back at the fall of ancient empires to the restoration of Chinese power, he argues we urgently need a new conception of power.

"Simply astonishing." — David Wengrow
events.title: The End of Nations

Gleeson is a comic making big, juicy, turbulent waves; run for cover. No one is safe.

"The makings of a star comedian." – Beyond The Joke

Self-optimisation is making us miserable, and someone needs to say so. One of the FT's sharpest columnists, Jemima Kelly, has spent years skewering Silicon Valley and wellness culture. Join her as she argues the case that the relentless measuring of everything is hollowing out the things that make life worth living.

events.title: Good Death Innovators: AI Beyond the Grave

events.description:
From Hollywood to Hegel, many have drawn comfort from the idea that history has a moral direction, and that “the good” will win out in the end. This thinking has influenced Marxist movements and shapes current progressive appeals to being on “the right side of history." But while the view that there is a moral direction to progress has traditionally won out, there is strong evidence that this is a mistake. Communist systems collapsed into nightmares. Liberal democracies have decayed. Recurring contemporary crises — pandemics, wars, climate change, and technological upheaval — leave us directionless. Increasingly it seems the good does not win out and social change fails not only to guarantee progress but lacks any moral direction at all.

Should we see moral and social progress as a dangerous fantasy from which we need to escape? Is the idea of a direction to history simply a means to justify our prejudices? Or is progress essential if we are to create purpose in a universe that otherwise offers no promise or triumph?

Titan of the radical left Tariq Ali, leading Chinese intellectual Wang Hui, and celebrated economic historian Deirdre McCloskey debate whether history has a moral direction.
events.speakers: Deirdre McCloskey, Wang Hui, Tariq Ali. Jack Symes hosts
events.title: Hollywood, Hegel and the Myth of the Good

events.description:
In the battle between the human desire for risk and the desire for safety, being safe has been the clear winner. By every measurable standard, humanity has never been safer. Global conflict deaths have plummeted from 300 to 1 per 100,000 between the 17th century and today. Child mortality has fallen from one in three to less than one in twenty. Tracking threats has undeniably saved lives. Yet, despite the data, many remain convinced we are living in an era of unprecedented peril. For two decades, Gallup found that most Americans believed crime was rising, even as FBI records showed it in freefall. We have built entire industries, government agencies, and daily protocols around predicting and mitigating danger — and the resulting hyper-vigilance some argue has left us paralysed by panic.

In trying to eliminate every danger, have we manufactured a culture of fear that stops us from living? Should we seek to reverse safety culture and cultivate a desire for risk? Or should the saved lives speak for themselves, and current anxieties a rational response to unpredictable, modern threats?

Heterodox sociologist Frank Furedi, celebrated statistician David Spiegelhalter, and Deputy Leader of the Green Party Rachel Millward debate danger, safety, and risk.
events.speakers: Frank Furedi, Rachel Millward, David Spiegelhalter. Jay Shapiro hosts
events.title: Danger and Risk in an Anxious World

events.description:
Floods, fires and failed harvests were supposed to jolt democracies into climate action. Instead, climate disasters, through fuelling political and economic discontent, are lighting a fire under the very anger that has empowered anti-climate populists. Who, in turn, then further slow the energy transition, driving worse disasters still. A doom loop in which the crisis erodes our capacity to respond to it. Join winner of the Commonwealth Prize and radical author of After Nations, Rana Dasgupta, for a live recording of the Overshoot podcast alongside host Laurie Laybourn, as they explore how to break free of the climate doom loop.

"The twenty-first century’s counterpart to Hobbes’ Leviathan." – Emmanuele Coccia
events.title: Breaking Free of the Doom Loop

events.description:
A split-hour comedy set from the brilliant Jen Nolan and hilarious Chantel Nash. Jen Nolan was hand-picked to perform in the highly acclaimed Comedy Reserve Show for Pleasance Theatres, and performed every night at the Edinburgh Festival this August. While Chantel Nash has shared the stage with some of the biggest names in UK Comedy, including Romesh Ranganathan and Judi Love, and supported Russell Kane and Josh Widdicombe on their most recent tours.

"[Chantel Nash] is a fast-rising future star of comedy. One you will certainly want to see." – Off The Kerb
events.title: Jen Nolan & Chantel Nash

events.description:
Green Man Festival alumni with major NME acclaim, Eve Appleton Band is fronted by exceptional singer-songwriter Eve Appleton-Scott. This rising alt-folk powerhouse has captured the industry's attention with their striking debut album Bible Black. Combining intricate storytelling with rich, multi-instrumental arrangements, they are a captivating new force on the scene.

“Almost impossible not to dance to.” – Warm Sounds
events.title: Eve Appleton Band

events.description: For billions of years, the ocean shaped life on Earth, its creatures evolving an extraordinary range of skills. But can intelligence exist without resembling our own? Meet octopuses with nine brains and fish whose collective decision-making proves the wisdom of crowds.
events.title: Ocean Intelligence

profiles.bio:
“I’m potentially the most measured person in human history."

Joining HowTheLightGetsIn from California, Bryan Johnson is a entrepreneur and venture capitalist turned self-declared immortality pioneer. The founder of payments company Braintree, sold to PayPal for $800 million in 2013, Johnson has spent his fortune on a stranger and more audacious project than anything Silicon Valley has seen: attempting to reverse his own biological age, and persuading the rest of humanity to follow him.

Project Blueprint, his $2 million-a-year regimen of diet, supplements, and experimental therapies, has made Johnson the world's most documented human guinea pig. He wakes at 4:30am, takes approximately 100 pills daily, submits every measurable system of his body to algorithmic optimisation, and broadcasts every biomarker to his millions of followers. His physicians claim the data shows measurable age reversal. His book Don't Die and We the People explore the new frontiers of being human.

"Johnson... has made himself a human guinea pig" — TIME Magazine
profiles.name: Bryan Johnson
profiles.tagline: Silicon Valley's Prophet of Immortality

profiles.bio:
"Quantum mechanics makes absolutely no sense."
Awarded the 2020 Nobel Prize in Physics for his work on black holes, Roger Penrose is a world-renowned mathematician and physicist. In recent years, he has investigated the relationship between physics and the mind, famously arguing that quantum mechanics plays an essential role in solving the mysteries of human consciousness.
Penrose has made numerous appearances on media such as BBC, Closer to Truth, and The Joe Rogan Experience. In 1994, he was knighted for his services to science.
"He is one of the very few people I've met in my life who, without reservation, I call a genius" — Lee Smolin
profiles.name: Roger Penrose
profiles.tagline: Nobel Laureate in Physics

profiles.bio:
“It has become more and more clear to me that to successfully address the big problems we face today, we need not only an entrepreneurial state and mission-oriented policies but also a new economics of collective action around the common good."
Professor in the Economics of Innovation and Public Value, University College London, Founding Director at the UCL Institute for Innovation and Public Purpose. Author of The Common Good Economy: a new compass.
Her latest book argues that economics lacks a coherent theory of the common good — and that doing good cannot remain a correction for market failure, but must become an objective we design and work towards together. Built around a practical "common good compass," the book sets out how governments, business and citizens can move from correcting mistakes to shaping outcomes, from tackling inequality to the climate crisis.

Mazzucato is also the author of The Entrepreneurial State, The Value of Everything, Mission Economy, and The Big Con. She advises policymakers around the world on innovation-led inclusive and sustainable growth, including as Chair of the World Health Organization's Council on the Economics of Health for All, Co-Chair of the Global Commission on the Economics of Water, and Special Adviser to South Africa's G20 Presidency. In 2021, she received the Grande Ufficiale Ordine al Merito della Repubblica Italiana from the Italian President – Italy's highest civilian honour.

"I believe [her vision] can help to think about the future." – Pope Francis
profiles.name: Mariana Mazzucato
profiles.tagline: Author of The Common Good Economy; Professor at University College London

profiles.bio:
"Imagine a world in which every single person on the planet is given free access to the sum of all human knowledge. That's what we're doing."

Jimmy Wales is an American internet entrepreneur and digital visionary best known for founding Wikipedia, the world’s largest collaborative encyclopedia. A pioneer of open knowledge, Wales has been a central figure in shaping the architecture and ethics of the modern internet, advancing the idea that information should be freely accessible to all.

Through the Wikimedia Foundation, which he founded to support Wikipedia and its sister projects, Wales helped establish a volunteer-driven model of knowledge creation grounded in neutrality, transparency, and public service. His work has influenced debates on digital commons, online governance, and the future of information in democratic societies.

"From the beginning, astonishingly revolutionary." — Rory Stewart

events.title: The Life and Philosophy of Jimmy Wales
Reality in the Age of Perspective

profiles.name: Jimmy Wales
profiles.tagline: Founder of Wikipedia

profiles.bio:
Louis Theroux is a genre-defining documentary filmmaker and presenter best known for his immersive and empathetic programmes exploring the intricate and often contentious facets of human existence.
These include his BAFTA-winning series Louis Theroux’s Weird Weekends and When Louis Met…, alongside a string of acclaimed and award-winning documentaries such as The Most Hated Family in America, Miami Mega Jail, Altered States, and the feature-length film My Scientology Movie.
In his BBC series Louis Theroux Interviews, he turned his attention to the world of celebrity, gaining rare access to some of entertainment’s most iconic figures and prompting revealing, unexpected conversations.
In 2025 Louis released Settlers, a documentary which examined the growing community of religious-nationalist Israelis who have settled in the occupied West Bank.
His latest documentary, Louis Theroux: Inside the Manosphere, premiered on Netflix this year.
The Louis Theroux Podcast launched in 2023. Each episode features an in-depth conversation between Louis and a fascinating guest including Shania Twain, PinkPantheress, Tracey Emin, Willem Dafoe, Steve Coogan to name a few.
Louis has won numerous awards, including three BAFTAs, an RTS award, and the 2019 Grierson’s Trustees’ Award. He co-founded the television production company Mindhouse alongside Arron Fellows and Nancy Strang.
profiles.name: Louis Theroux
profiles.tagline: Genre-defining documentary filmmaker

profiles.bio:
"The Holy Grail is...trying to understand a theory of quantum gravity."

Tipped as the next Einstein, Sabrina Gonzalez Pasterski is a pioneering theoretical physicist reshaping our understanding of space, time, and gravity. A first-generation Cuban-American from Chicago, she built and flew her own plane solo at 14, graduated from MIT with a perfect 5.0 GPA, and earned her PhD from Harvard, where her early work on the spin memory effect was later cited by Stephen Hawking. She has received job offers from NASA and Jeff Bezos' Blue Origin, and was named to Forbes' 30 Under 30 list twice.

Now a faculty member at the Perimeter Institute and founder and principal investigator of the Celestiail Holography Initiative, Pasterski leads efforts to encode the universe as a hologram, a bold step toward uniting quantum theory with general relativity.

"Her potential is off the charts." — Allen Haggerty, MIT

events.title: The Hype and The Limits of AI
The Holographic Universe and The Rise of AI Physics

profiles.name: Sabrina Pasterski
profiles.tagline: Theoretical Physicist Tipped as Next Einstein

profiles.bio:
“If you put us in a difficult corner, we will stand our ground—that is the kind of country we are.”
Former Chancellor of the Exchequer Jeremy Hunt is a leading Conservative politician and one of the longest-serving Cabinet ministers of his generation, having also held senior roles as Secretary of State for Health and Secretary of State for Foreign Affairs. During his record-breaking six years as Health Secretary, Hunt became one of the most controversial and consequential figures in NHS history. Known for stepping in to stabilise the economy during recent market turbulence, he has consistently championed a pragmatic, centrist conservatism.
Hunt has remained an active public voice on healthcare, public finance, and British competitiveness. His recent book, Can We Be Great Again? Why a Dangerous World Needs Britain, broadens his purview to grand strategy, arguing for a renewed, confident UK international presence in an increasingly volatile era.
“Jeremy Hunt points the way to how we British can recover our confidence—at a crucial time in world affairs when we are going to need it.” — William Hague
profiles.name: Jeremy Hunt
profiles.tagline: Former Chancellor of the Exchequer

profiles.bio:
“I talk to many kinds of guests. Listening does not mean I agree with them.”

Dasha Nekrasova is a filmmaker and podcast host who has become a prominent and provocative voice in contemporary media. Today, she is best known as the co-host of the cultural commentary podcast Red Scare, where she continuously pushes the boundaries of modern social and political discourse.

She gained mainstream recognition for her recurring role on HBO's acclaimed series Succession. In 2021, she made her directorial debut with The Scary of Sixty-First, a thriller she also co-wrote and starred in, which went on to win the Best First Feature Award at the Berlin International Film Festival.

"Dasha Nekrasova Believes in God, Wellbutrin, and Sigmund Freud" — Interview Magazine
profiles.name: Dasha Nekrasova
profiles.tagline: Succession Star Turned Cultural Provocateur

profiles.bio:
"Most of all we want our—and Britain’s—future back"

Torsten Bell is a politician, author and economist  currently serving as Labour MP for Swansea West. He was the leader of the Resolution Foundation between 2015 and 2024, a charity working to raise the living standards of low-income households. Writing regularly on issues of poverty and inequality, Bell was a prominent opponent of the September 2022 United Kingdom mini-budget and a critic of the levelling-up policy of the 2019 Conservative government.

Bell's latest book Great Britain? How We Get Our Future Back is a Sunday Times bestseller, offering a clear-eyed portrait of the inequality and stagnant economic growth facing Britain—as well as an optimistic vision of economic growth.

"A dose of Torstenomics is the only thing that can give us hope" — Amol Rajan
profiles.name: Torsten Bell
profiles.tagline: Leading Labour MP and Government Pensions Minister

profiles.bio:
“Humans think they are free, conscious beings, when in truth they are deluded animals."

John Gray, hailed as "Britain's best philosopher," is a leading critic of liberalism and the Enlightenment. He has long challenged the belief in inevitable progress, predicting both the 2008 financial crisis and the rise of populism. Celebrated and controversial, Gray's provocative writing has been hailed by George Soros "for its powerful analysis of the deepening instability of global capitalism.”

He is the bestselling author of Straw Dogs, The Silence of Animals, and Seven Types of Atheism as well as a frequent contributor to The Guardian, New Statesman, and The Times Literary Supplement. Gray’s sharp insights and contrarian stance continue to shape contemporary debates on ethics, politics, and the future of humanity.

"One of the most important thinkers alive." — ​The Times
profiles.name: John Gray
profiles.tagline: Philosopher Exposing Humanism as Religious Delusion

profiles.bio:
"Poets are not to blame for how things are.”
Joining HowTheLightGetsIn from Pennsylvania, Emily Wilson is a celebrated writer and classicist whose translations of Homer have reshaped how ancient literature reaches contemporary readers. In 2018, she became the first woman to translate Homer’s Odyssey into English verse; her acclaimed translation of The Iliad followed in 2023. She is Department Chair and Professor of Classical Studies at the University of Pennsylvania, where she holds the College for Women Class of 1963 Term Professorship in the Humanities.
She has been named a Fellow of the American Academy in Rome in Renaissance & Early Modern scholarship, a MacArthur Fellow, and a Guggenheim Fellow. Her forthcoming book, Crossing the Wine-Dark Sea, explores the enduring afterlives of Homer and the ways stories travel across time.
"Joyful, illuminating, and engrossing." — Madeline Miller
profiles.name: Emily Wilson
profiles.tagline: First Woman to Translate the Odyssey Into English

profiles.bio:
"I find philosophy—philosophy in the largest sense—a profoundly concrete, sensual activity."
Galen Strawson is a British philosopher renowned for his work on consciousness, the self, and the limits of human freedom. Currently Professor of Philosophy at the University of Texas at Austin, Strawson is one of the most distinguished voices in contemporary analytic philosophy.
Strawson is best known for his defence of panpsychism—the view that consciousness is a fundamental feature of reality—as well as his influential critique of the idea of moral responsibility in “The Impossibility of Moral Responsibility.” He has also challenged conventional ideas of personal identity, arguing that many people do not experience themselves as persisting “selves” over time.
"Galen Strawson opens windows and finds light-switches like no other philosopher writing today." — Stephen Fry
profiles.name: Galen Strawson
profiles.tagline: Pioneering Philosopher of Panpsychism

profiles.bio:
"The focus on all forms of trauma except economic exploitation has helped to disguise the problem at the heart of neoliberalism."
Firebrand intellectual Catherine Liu is a professor of Film and Media Studies at the University of California, Irvine, renowned for her incisive critiques of contemporary cultural and political dynamics. Her scholarly work delves into the intersections of critical theory, political economy, and cultural criticism.
Liu's most recent book is Traumatized: The New Politics of Public Suffering. In it, she argues that our current politics mistakes emotional display for political action. Her other publications include Virtue Hoarders: The Case Against the Professional Managerial Class (2021), a polemical examination of the class's role in perpetuating economic and social inequalities, and The American Idyll: Academic Anti-Elitism as Cultural Critique (2011), which explores the complexities of anti-elitism in American cultural politics.
"Liu’s comments in Virtue Hoarders on politics seem spot-on."—The Independent Review

events.title: Champagne, Cake and Philosophy with Catherine Liu

profiles.name: Catherine Liu
profiles.tagline: Left-wing critic of the progressive elite

profiles.bio:
"Any nation that underuses the potential of women, that underuses half its population, is needlessly impoverishing itself."

Nicola Sturgeon is a Scottish politician who served as First Minister of Scotland and Leader of the Scottish National Party from 2014 to 2023, becoming one of Europe's most prominent political figures. Sturgeon has shaped defining debates in modern Britain — from Scottish independence to Brexit — and introduced bold policies including the Scottish Child Payment and world-leading climate targets. 

Sturgeon published her candid memoir Frankly, an instant Sunday Times bestseller, in August 2025. 

"[Nicola Sturgeon] is a model to women everywhere" — Nancy Pelosi, 52nd Speaker of the United States House of Representatives

events.title: Winning and Losing on the Global Stage

profiles.name: Nicola Sturgeon
profiles.tagline: Longest-Serving First Minister of Scotland

profiles.bio:
"All this chaos. It's part of who I am."

Jordan Stephens is a British artist, actor, and mental health advocate, best known as one-half of the chart-topping hip-hop duo Rizzle Kicks. The group succeeded with hits like “Down with the Trumpets” and performed at major festivals, including Glastonbury.

Beyond music, Stephens is an advocate for men’s mental health, speaking openly about emotional well-being and challenging traditional notions of masculinity. He has also acted in TV series such as Glue, Catastrophe, and Feel Good, and films like Rogue One and Teen Spirit. His latest book, Avoidance, Drugs, Heartbreak explores the struggles of a young man rising to fame.

"Brutally honest as well as poetic" — Dolly Alderton

events.title: Life, the Self, and the Infinite Scroll
The Philosophy and the Dangers of Fame

profiles.name: Jordan Stephens
profiles.tagline: Hip Hop Star and Mental Health Advocate

profiles.bio:
"Theoretical physicists used to explain what was observed. Now they try to explain why they can't explain what was not observed."
Fearlessly critical of current physics research, Sabine Hossenfelder is a theoretical physicist who specialises in the foundations of science and has become a celebrated science communicator, bestselling author, and independent researcher. Her recent books include Lost in Math: How Beauty Leads Physics Astray, and the New York Times's Best Selling Existential Physics: A Scientist's Guide to Life's Biggest Questions.
Hossenfelder is the creator behind the popular YouTube channel, "Science without the gobbledygook." which has amassed over one million subscribers. Her writing has featured in some of the world's top publications, including Scientific American, New Scientist, and Nautilus.
“A physicist who is utterly fearless, completely honest, and quite funny.” — Peter Woit
profiles.name: Sabine Hossenfelder
profiles.tagline: Science's Biggest Reality Checker

profiles.bio:
"London does not belong to Labour. It does not belong to the Tories. It belongs to the people."

Laila Cunningham is a former Crown Prosecution Service prosecutor turned Reform UK figurehead, whose defection from the Conservative Party in June 2025 made her the first Reform sitting councillor in a London borough. A fierce critic of establishment failures on crime, immigration, and free speech, she has rapidly become one of the most prominent new voices on the British right.

In January 2026 Nigel Farage announced her as Reform UK's candidate for the London Mayoralty in 2028 and head of London campaigning. 

“Laila is an enormously talented, successful woman" — Nigel Farage
profiles.name: Laila Cunningham
profiles.tagline: Reform UK's Face of London

profiles.bio:
“Conversion and zealotry, just like revelation and apostasy, are flip sides of the same coin, the currency of a political culture having more in common with religion than rational discourse.” 

Norman Finkelstein is one of the most high-profile political scientists writing today. The son of Holocaust survivors, he earned his doctorate in politics from Princeton and spent decades teaching political theory and the Israel-Palestine conflict before his tenure bid at DePaul University was denied in 2007, following a widely publicisedfeud with Harvard's Alan Dershowitz.

One of America's most controversial political commentators, Finkelstein is the author of more than a dozen books, translated into over fifty foreign editions, including Image and Reality of the Israel–Palestine Conflict, Beyond Chutzpah: On the Misuse of Anti-Semitism and the Abuse of History, and Gaza: An Inquest into Its Martyrdom. His most recent book, Gaza's Gravediggers: An Inquiry into Corruption in High Places, turns his forensic scrutiny on the international institutions and intellectuals he accuses of enabling the war in Gaza.

"A brave and brilliant truth-teller.” — John Mearsheimer

events.title: The Code for Good and Evil

profiles.name: Norman Finkelstein
profiles.tagline: America's Most Contested Voice on the Middle East

profiles.bio:
Michael Gove is the Editor of The Spectator. As the former Member of Parliament for Surrey Heath and UK Government Cabinet Minister, he served in Cabinet across five government departments for more than a decade, from the 2010 Coalition government onwards.
 
As Secretary of State for Education, he steered through some of the biggest changes to education in half a century. He went on to serve in the cabinets of three of the four subsequent Prime Ministers, including as Chief Whip, Chancellor of the Duchy of Lancaster, Secretary of State for Justice, for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs and for Levelling Up, Housing and Communities.
 
In May 2025, Michael was made a peer in Rishi Sunak’s honours list and joined the House of Lords, choosing the title of Lord Gove of Torry.
Photo credit: Roger Harris

events.title: The Life and Philosophy of Michael Gove
The Rise and Fall of the Educated Elite
The Nation State vs Big Tech

profiles.name: Michael Gove
profiles.tagline: Leading Figure in Tory Cabinet 2010-2024

profiles.bio:
"The 21st century will be the Asian century."

Kishore Mahbubani is a Singaporean diplomat, scholar, and global thinker who has spent his career urging the West to see the world through non-Western eyes. Former President of the United Nations Security Council and Singapore's former Ambassador to the UN, Mahbubani is among Asia's most influential voices on geopolitics and the shifting balance of global power.

Mahbubani has shaped the intellectual debate on what he calls "the great convergence" — the historic return of Asia to the global center stage. His books, including Has the West Lost It? and The Asian 21st Century, have been translated worldwide and taught in universities from Beijing to Boston.

“There is no more thoughtful observer of Asia, the United States, and their interaction than Kishore Mahbubani.” — Larry Summers

events.title: Five Fatal Fallacies of the West

profiles.name: Kishore Mahbubani
profiles.tagline: Former Singaporean Ambassador and President of UN Security Council

profiles.bio:
"If we assume from the start that everything mental must be reducible to something physical, then we close the possibility of understanding the mind on its own terms"

Victoria Trumbull is a philosopher, researcher, and writer who challenges the dominance of reductive materialism in contemporary thought. Working across philosophical psychology, metaphysics, and the history of ideas, she seeks to recover a deeper, more expansive understanding of the human soul.

Her recent essays and public philosophy argue that memory is not stored in the brain but unfolds in time, offering a powerful alternative to prevailing neuroscience-led accounts of mind and bringing renewed attention to the interior dimensions of human experience.

"Ms Trumbull is doing something very different, finding in philosophers of the past—and in two very different ones—the resources to develop philosophy today in a promising new direction." — Professor John Marenbon

events.title: The Self, The Soul, and the Nature of Reality

profiles.name: Victoria Trumbull
profiles.tagline: Philosopher Challenging Materialist Consensus

profiles.bio:
“Intolerance blooms in the soil of our faulty logic.” 

Rebecca Goldstein is a philosopher and novelist. Her most recent book, The Mattering Instinct: How Our Deepest Longing Drives Us and Divides Us, argues that the need to matter is the source of our greatest progress as well as our deepest conflicts, and is the very crux of the human experience. She holds a PhD in philosophy of science from Princeton and has taught at Yale, Columbia, NYU, Dartmouth, and Harvard.

Goldstein has won a MacArthur ​“Genius” Award as well as the National Jewish Book Award, and in 2014 was presented with the National Humanities Medal by Barak Obama. She has written ten books, both fiction and nonfiction, including Thirty-Six Arguments for the Existence of God: A Work of Fiction, Plato at the Googleplex: Why Philosophy Won't Go Away, and two biographical studies, one on Gödel and another on Spinoza.

"Rebecca Goldstein helps us to see that so much of our lives, and so much of human history, is driven by the need to matter" — Jonathan Haidt
profiles.name: Rebecca Goldstein
profiles.tagline: Award-Winning Philosopher and Novelist

profiles.bio:
"I don’t like the idea that people ‘ought’ to have a particular political philosophy because they are brown, or white, or female or gay"

Leo Varadkar is one of the defining Irish political figures of his generation. He served twice as Taoiseach (Prime Minister) of Ireland — from June 2017 to Jun 2020, and again from December 2022 to April 2024 — making history as the country's first openly gay Taoiseach. He governed through a period of rapid social change, including the marriage equality referendum, Brexit, and the pandemic. 

Varadkar is the author of the candid memoir Speaking My Mind, in which he reflects on leadership, identity, and marriage equality. Since leaving frontline politics, he has become Senior Fellow for the Global LGBTQI+ Human Rights Program at the Harvard Kennedy School. 

"A transformative period in Irish and global politics" - Mary Regan

events.title: The Nation State vs Big Tech

profiles.name: Leo Varadkar
profiles.tagline: Former Prime Minister of Ireland

profiles.bio:
"I don’t write fiction for people to identify with and I don’t write a picture of the world they can recognise. I write to astonish people.”

Will Self is a satirist, novelist, journalist, cultural critic and one of Britain's most provocative literary voices. Honorary Professor of Contemporary Thought at Brunel University London, Self has written more than two dozen books spanning satirical fiction, memoir, and non-fiction. His novel Umbrella was shortlisted for the Man Booker Prize, and his books have been translated into more than twenty languages. A longtime contributor to The Guardian, the London Review of Books, Harper's Magazine and The New York Times, he has been a columnist for The Observer, The Times, The New Statesman, the Evening Standard, and The New European.

His most recent novel, The Quantity Theory of Morality, is a savage satire of the English middle class and Anglo-European liberal elite. It follows his novel Elaine, which draws on the diaries of his late mother — part autofiction, part feminist portrait of a woman crushed by post-war domesticity.

"Self is the most daring and delightful novelist of his generation" ― Guardian

events.title: The End of the Book: A Civilisation in Crisis

profiles.name: Will Self
profiles.tagline: Britain's Leading Literary Provocateur

profiles.bio:
"You have no beginning of time. It's always been there."

Neil Turok is a theoretical physicist and cosmologist who has spent his career asking the most fundamental question in science: how did the universe begin? He is best known for his quantum-cosmology calculations with Stephen Hawking, and for the cyclic-universe and ekpyrotic models developed with Paul Steinhardt, theories that directly challenge the dominant model of cosmic inflation. His most recent work proposes a "mirror universe": the idea that a parallel anti-universe, moving backwards in time from our perspective, was pulled into existence alongside our own at the moment of the Big Bang. 

He has held professorships at Princeton and the Chair of Mathematical Physics at Cambridge, and has held the Higgs Chair of Theoretical Physics at the University of Edinburgh since 2020. He has been awarded the TED Prize for his work in mathematical physics and in establishing the African Institute for Mathematical Sciences in Muizenberg. In 2026, he was elected a Fellow of the Royal Society in recognition of his groundbreaking work in theoretical physics. 

"I have been very impressed by his insight and originality." — Stephen Hawking

events.title: The Big Bang Hides A Mirror Universe

profiles.name: Neil Turok
profiles.tagline: Physicist Uncovering the Origins of the Universe

profiles.bio:
“The fake outrage of academic philosophy amazes me.”

Tommy J. Curry is the Personal Chair of Africana Philosophy and Black Male Studies at the University of Edinburgh, renowned for his critical scholarship on the intersection of race, gender, and power. He was awarded the prestigious American Book Award for his groundbreaking book The Man Not, which dismantles prevailing narratives by arguing that Black masculinity is not a mimicry of white patriarchy but a unique and oppositional identity.

Curry’s work has been hailed by scholars as “required reading for all who work at the intersection of race and gender, especially in the current political milieu,” and he continues to challenge academic orthodoxy through his fierce public interventions, teaching, and edited volumes in Africana philosophy.

“Tommy Curry challenges the cozy consensus among self-conceived progressives in the humanities…  required reading for anyone interested in understanding oppression or having unquestioned assumptions put to the test." —Charles W. Mills, Distinguished Professor at the City University of New York Graduate Center

events.title: The Code for Good and Evil

profiles.name: Tommy Curry
profiles.tagline: Critic of White Progressive Orthodoxy

profiles.bio:
“We can be blind to the obvious, and we are also blind to our blindness.”

Gillian Tett is one of the world's most influential interpreters of global finance and power. She is one of the few leading economists who predicted the 2008 financial crisis. In her famous 2009 book Fool's Gold, she recounts how a  tightly bonded team of bankers — the "Morgan Mafia" — triggered the global recession. 

Tett is a member of the editorial board and columnist at the Financial Times, where her reporting and commentary bridge economics, politics, and culture. In 2023, she was appointed Provost of King's College, Cambridge. She is the author of Fool's Gold, The Silo Effect, and Anthro-Vision.

"Absolutely brilliant" — Daniel Kahnehman
profiles.name: Gillian Tett
profiles.tagline: World-Leading Journalist Who Predicted the 2008 Crisis

profiles.bio:
"Proximity to power has an unsurprising ability to mutate a politician's spinal cord into bright yellow jelly.”

A leading figure on the radical left for over six decades, Tariq Ali is a renowned writer, filmmaker, and public intellectual. A longtime editor at New Left Review, author of more than 50 books and frequent contributor to The Guardian, CounterPunch, and the London Review of Books, his influence on the intellectual landscape of the left cannot be overstated.

Born in Lahore and educated at Oxford, where he led the Oxford Union and became a figurehead of the 1960s anti-Vietnam War movement, Ali has remained one of the Anglophone left's most independent voices—equally willing to challenge Western liberalism and the failures of postcolonial states. His vast body of work—spanning fiction, history, and polemic—includes The Clash of Fundamentalism, Winston Churchill: His Times, His Crime, and his Islam Quintet of novels.

"Ali remains an outlier and intellectual bomb-thrower; an urbane, Oxford-educated polemicist." — The Observer

events.title: Hollywood, Hegel and the Myth of the Good

profiles.name: Tariq Ali
profiles.tagline: Titan of the Radical Left

profiles.bio:
"Everyone pursues their national interests. The only one who gets blamed for it is the United States."

Joining HowTheLightGetsIn from America, John Bolton is an American attorney, diplomat, and one of the leading voices in modern American foreign policy. A lifelong defender of American power, Bolton served as the 26th United States National Security Advisor to President Donald Trump from April 2018 to September 2019, having previously served as the interim United States Ambassador to the United Nations from 2005 to 2006.

A Yale-trained lawyer and veteran of the Reagan and both Bush administrations, he has spent decades championing a muscular, interventionist foreign policy. He is the bestselling author of The Room Where It Happened: A White House Memoir, a searing insider account of his time in the Trump administration, as well as Surrender Is Not an Option and How Barack Obama is Endangering our National Sovereignty.

"No one understands the enemies of America and the threat to our survival better than Ambassador John Bolton" — Newt Gingrich

events.title: Winning and Losing on the Global Stage

profiles.name: John Bolton
profiles.tagline: Former US National Security Advisor

profiles.bio:
"Revolutionary politics is the only way we can save ourselves...But it has to begin with the recognition and criticalization of the actual and specific forms of power"

Divya Dwivedi is an Indian philosopher and professor at the Indian Institute of Technology, Delhi, working across continental philosophy, critical theory, narratology, and the critical philosophy of caste and race. Her thinking has developed in dialogue with some of the most significant thinkers of our time — including Slavoj Žižek, Étienne Balibar, and the late Jean-Luc Nancy — and her philosophical dismantling of upper-caste supremacism has drawn international acclaim. 

Her latest book, Indian Philosophy, Indian Revolution: On Caste and Politics (co-authored with Shaj Mohan), calls for revolutionary transformation within India’s caste system, which Žižek called "required reading for anyone who wants to understand the precipice toward which our entire world is heading."

"Not since the days of Sartre has philosophy addressed political issues with the directness and clarity that Dwivedi and Mohan bring." — Robert Bernasconi

events.title: The Real Gandhi Behind the Western Myth

profiles.name: Divya Dwivedi
profiles.tagline: Philosopher Dismantling 1,000 Years of Caste Ideology

profiles.bio:
“Every human being, in a way, is a philosopher. Because that's what it is to be human.”

Hilary Lawson is a philosopher, renowned critic of philosophical realism and editorial director of the Institute of Art and Ideas. His main work, Closure: A Story of Everything, has been described as ‘the first non-realist metaphysics’.

His early work made the case that twentieth-century philosophy was centrally concerned with the paradoxes of self-reference. Closure can be seen as an attempt to resolve these paradoxes and at the same time to provide an account of language that does require reference to an external reality. In doing so it outlines a metaphysics that abandons the traditional relationship between language and the world in favour of a vocabulary of closure and openness. The theory has dramatic consequences for how we understand ourselves and the world, and the role of both science and religion.

“Lawson shows himself to be a latter-day 'metaphysician' on the grand scale ... a quite astonishing achievement.” — Alan Montefiore, University of Oxford

events.title: The Hype and The Limits of AI
The Self, The Soul, and the Nature of Reality

profiles.name: Hilary Lawson
profiles.tagline: Post-postmodern philosopher

profiles.bio:
"We are often told that capitalism is in crisis, but look around the world and you'll see that it has never been so buoyant."

Kwasi Kwarteng is a former Conservative politician, historian, and author who served as Chancellor of the Exchequer under Liz Truss in 2022. He holds a PhD in economic history and worked as a journalist and financial analyst before going into politics.

A prolific author, his books include Ghosts of Empire: Britain's Legacies in the Modern World and Britannia Unchained, alongside works on debt, Thatcherism, and the history of capitalism.

"Smart, witty and personable" ― Daily Telegraph
profiles.name: Kwasi Kwarteng
profiles.tagline: Historian and Former Chancellor Under Liz Truss

profiles.bio:
"When Galileo invented the telescope, people didn't want to look through it...people [now] refuse to look at certain theories [too]."

Ivette Fuentes is a Professor of Quantum Physics at the University of Southampton and Emmy Fellow at Keble College, University of Oxford. Her work considers fundamental quantum mechanics, quantum optics and their interplay with general relativity. Fuentes' work has appeared in New Scientist and she participated in a BBC series Magic Numbers with Hannah Fry. Fuentes is a close collaborator of Roger Penrose.

Fuentes' work tests theories of quantum gravity by developing much of the under-researched experimental input and quantum technology at scales where quantum and relativistic effects coexist.

"I lost count of how many pioneering ideas [Ivette has given] with actual practical consequences in the near term."— Curt Jaimungal

events.title: Darwin's Physics and the Evolving Universe

profiles.name: Ivette Fuentes
profiles.tagline: Leading Quantum Physicist

profiles.bio:
“For all its benefits, technology restricted our experiential horizons"

Audrey Borowski is a researcher and author, specialising in the philosophy of artificial intelligence. She has held numerous fellowships, most notably at the Max Planck Institute for the History of Science in Berlin. She is currently a Leverhulme Early Career Fellow and Isaac Newton Trust Fellow at the University of Cambridge.

A regular contributor to the Times Literary Supplement and Aeon, she is the author of Leibniz in His World: The Making of a Savant, which provides a groundbreaking reassessment of Leibniz, painting a nuanced portrait of him as an aspiring scientist and courtier, challenging the image of Leibniz as an isolated genius. Her current research and upcoming book project explores the topics of data, algorithmic systems and ideology.

"A startlingly fine piece of original, lucid, and brilliant scholarly work." — Jacob Soll, author of The Free Market: The History of an Idea

events.title: The Hype and The Limits of AI
Power in the Age of AI

profiles.name: Audrey Borowski
profiles.tagline: Leverhulme Fellow Rewriting the Philosophy of AI

profiles.bio:
"Our project of civilization has been successful on scales we could not have imagined when we began it ten millennia ago. But with that success has come consequences that will last for centuries."

Adam Frank is an American astrophysicist, writer, and public intellectual who serves as Professor of Physics and Astronomy at the University of Rochester. His scientific work probes the birth and death of stars: his research group developed advanced supercomputer tools to simulate how stars form and how they end their lives.

Frank is also a widely read cultural commentator on science. He co-founded the NPR blog Cosmos and Culture and now writes for the Big Think blog. His books, including Light of the Stars and The Blind Spot, explore what our cosmic discoveries might teach us about our future on Earth, the fragility of civilization, and the deep questions linking science, life, and human meaning.

"Adam Frank ably picks up where Carl Sagan left off." — Andrew Revkin
profiles.name: Adam Frank
profiles.tagline: Trailblazing Astrophysicist

profiles.bio:
"The system that causes the climate crisis is the same system that causes the cost-of-living crisis."

Rachel Millward is Deputy Leader of the Green Party of England and Wales. She entered politics in 2021, winning the Hartfield seat on Wealden District Council from the Conservatives in a by-election by just 122 votes. She retained the seat in 2023 with an increased majority, and was appointed joint-leader of the council that same year, heading a coalition with the Liberal Democrats.

In 2025 Millward stood for the Green Party deputy leadership, and was elected joint deputy leader alongside Mothin Ali under the newly elected leader Zack Polanski, She is now the Green Party’s candidate for the inaugural Mayor of Sussex and Brighton in 2028.

"I know first-hand how driven Rachel is to make a tangible difference to people’s lives." — Zack Polanski

events.title: Danger and Risk in an Anxious World

profiles.name: Rachel Millward
profiles.tagline: Deputy Leader of the Green Party of England and Wales

profiles.bio:
"Things are not going back to ‘normal’: we are living through the end of the world as we’ve known it. How we choose to live will shape the next era."

Sarah Wilson is a multi-New York Times and Amazon bestselling author, social philosopher, international keynote speaker, minimalist and philanthropist. She edited Cosmopolitan magazine Australia at 29, founded the global I Quit Sugar movement, hosted the most-watched TV series in the nation’s history — Masterchef Australia — and wrote the bestseller First,We Make the Beast Beautiful. 

Her most recent book, I Eat the Stars: How to Live Fully and Beautifully in a Collapsing World, is a guide to finding meaning in a world that seems to be falling apart, and she has ranked in the top 200 most influential authors in the world (two years in a row).

"The wonderful Sarah Wilson writes straight to the beating heart of what we all need to hear." — Liam Neeson

events.title: The Philosophy and the Dangers of Fame
A Civilisational Collapse Like Any Other

profiles.name: Sarah Wilson
profiles.tagline: Anxiety's most articulate advocate

profiles.bio:
"Man in his hunt for objective reality suddenly discovered that he always confronts himself alone"

Thomas Hertog is a cosmologist and professor of theoretical physics at KU Leuven, Belgium, where he works on the quantum nature of black holes and the state of our early universe. A long time collaborator of Stephen Hawking's, Hertog has been questioning the status of our physical laws moments after the big bang. In his influential book, On the Origin of Time: Stephen Hawking's Final Theory, he challenges the mainstream conception that the laws of physics are immutable and instead proposes a Darwinian picture, where laws evolved with the universe.

Having held fellowships at UC Santa Barbara and CERN, Hertog also leads Belgium’s participation in the European Space Agency’s flagship mission dedicated to the detection of gravitational waves. He is a world-renowned science communicator and has curated several exhibitions combining art and science.

"A fascinating insight into one of humankind’s deepest quests, by one of its deepest minds." — Dr Christophe Galfard, author of The Universe in Your Hand and former student of Stephen Hawking.

events.title: Darwin's Physics and the Evolving Universe

profiles.name: Thomas Hertog
profiles.tagline: Hawking Collaborator Arguing the Laws of Physics Evolve

profiles.bio:
"Human life has a depth, a depth not found in nature."

Sebastian Rödl is a German philosopher and one of the most distinctive voices in contemporary European philosophy. Rödl's work focuses on the nature of human thought and self-consciousness. His book Self-Consciousness and Objectivity: An Introduction to Absolute Idealism, published by Harvard University Press, aims to transform our understanding of self-consciousness and its place in the world.

Rödl is Professor at the University of Leipzig. He has also been Visiting Scholar at the Department of Philosophy at UC Berkeley.

"Addresses the most essential questions about self-consciousness" — Berislav Marušić, Brandeis University

events.title: The Self Is Not In The World

profiles.name: Sebastian Rödl
profiles.tagline: German Philosopher Rewriting the Logic of Self-Consciousness

profiles.bio:
“To maintain and transmit a value system, human beings are punched, bullied, sent to gaol, thrown into concentration camps, cajoled, bribed, made into heroes… and sometimes even taught sociology”

Steven Lukes is a British political and social theorist. He held positions at Oxford, the London School of Economics, the University of Siena, and the European University before retiring as a professor at New York University in 2021. His contributions to the field have been widely recognised, including his election as a Fellow of the British Academy and the award of an honorary Doctor of Letters from the University of East Anglia. 

Lukes is best known for his influential work Power: A Radical View, in which he argues that power operates through three dimensions: decision-making, agenda-setting, and ideological power. His broader academic interests include individualism, moral conflict, rationality, relativism, and the sociology of Durkheim.

“Steven Lukes stirred up an intellectual firestorm.” – Michael Walzer

events.title: Power in the Age of AI

profiles.name: Steven Lukes
profiles.tagline: Political Theorist Redefining Power

profiles.bio:
“With each book you get a new fresh chance.” 

Patricia Lockwood is an American poet, novelist, and essayist widely regarded as one of the most original literary voices of her generation. A contributing editor at the London Review of Books, she is the only writer with both fiction and nonfiction works selected as the 10 Best Books of the Year by The New York Times. 

Lockwood is the bestselling author of the memoir Priestdaddy — named one of The Guardian’s 100 Best Books of the 21st Century — and the novels No One Is Talking About This, winner of the Dylan Thomas Prize and shortlisted for the Booker, and Will There Ever Be Another You, named one of The New Yorker’s Best Books of 2025. Her forthcoming poetry collection, Agate Head/Stone Soup, is published by Penguin in 2026. 

"A cultural critic at the height of her powers." — The Paris Review

events.title: Life, the Self, and the Infinite Scroll

profiles.name: Patricia Lockwood
profiles.tagline: Leading American Novelist and Critic

profiles.bio:
"I would keep as much of Neoclassical economics as modern astronomy kept of Ptolemaic astronomy — which is to say, nothing at all.” 

Steve Keen is one of the world's most provocative economists. Celebrated and controversial, Keen was one of the few economists to warn of the 2008 financial crisis, predicting as early as 2005 that the boom in private debt in developed countries was unsustainable. 

Keen is the author of several books including Debunking Economics, where he launches a full-range critique of Neoclassical economics. Keen argues that the support for doctrines such as free trade among economists is based on dogma, not rational argument or empirical evidence. Now an independent researcher, Keen holds the titles of Honorary Professor and Distinguished Research Fellow at UCL.

"No one is more qualified than Steve Keen to answer the question 'Can we avoid another financial crisis?'" ― Yanis Varoufakis

events.title: The Lie At The Heart of Economics

profiles.name: Steve Keen
profiles.tagline: Heterodox Economist

profiles.bio:
“We know of no path that will take us from where we are now, in terms of computing and AI technology, to the singularity.” 

Michael Wooldridge is a leading computer scientist and the Ashall Professor of Foundations of Artificial Intelligence at the University of Oxford, where he also services as Head of the Department of Computer Science. He is known for his pioneering work on multi-agent systems: systems composed of multiple self-interested intelligent agents that can cooperate, negotiate, and tackle complex problems. Having researched the field for decades, he is one of the world’s foremost authorities on AI.

He was awarded the prestigious Michael Faraday Prize by the Royal Society in late 2025 – awarded for excellence in science communication, and previously won by figures including David Attenborough. His book The Road to Conscious Machines offers an authoritative guide to AI past and present bringing “a healthy injection of humility to an overhyped field.”

“Michael Wooldridge is like the teacher you wish you’d had” — The Guardian

events.title: The Hype and The Limits of AI

profiles.name: Michael Wooldridge
profiles.tagline: Oxford Computer Scientist Unmasking the Limits of LLMs

profiles.bio:
"I try to think critically, question deeply, and laugh at the utter absurdity where I can."

Laura Kennedy is a writer, journalist, and philosopher with a PhD from Trinity College Dublin. Her writing has appeared in The Irish Times, The Sunday Times Style, The Guardian, Vogue, and Grazia, spanning philosophy and culture as readily as beauty and sport, and finding the ideas hiding inside both.

Her Substack, Peak Notions — described as "the ideologically exhausted person's guide to untangling ideas, identity, and the chaos we live in"  — has attracted tens of thousands of subscribers, by looking at the philosophical, cultural and social dynamics shaping our lives, and trying to make sense of them.

events.title: The Life and Philosophy of Jimmy Wales

profiles.name: Laura Kennedy
profiles.tagline: Philosopher and Writer Untangling How We Live

profiles.bio:
"I don't know why we think it's unfeminist to sexualise yourself in the public eye."

Farha Khalidi is a feminist cultural commentator, TikToker, and OnlyFans model known for her bold, unapologetic voice. With 1.7 million followers on TikTok, she challenges male-dominated power structures and champions women’s rights.

Farha gained wider recognition with appearances on shows like Piers Morgan Uncensored and Politics Joe, sparking conversations about feminism, the manosphere and self-expression.
profiles.name: Farha Khalidi
profiles.tagline: TikTok Feminist Firebrand

profiles.bio:
"If we only stick to our own echo chambers, wherever they are on the political spectrum, we change nothing and increase polarisation and mistrust.”

Thangam Debbonaire is a Labour member of the House of Lords, having served for nine years as MP for Bristol West and as a senior figure in Keir Starmer’s Shadow Cabinet. She held roles including Shadow Secretary of State for Culture, Media and Sport and Shadow Leader of the House of Commons, and previously served as Shadow Brexit Minister and a Labour Whip.

Since entering the Lords, Debbonaire’s work has focused on strategic advisory roles spanning arts and cultural diplomacy, tech and AI and the UN Sustainable Development Goals. She likes to take on controversial topics such as corporate donations, cultural reparations, migration, identity, and the future of democracy. 

"Thangam has a refreshing, independent outlook." —  Elaine Robinson

events.title: The Code for Good and Evil
The Rise and Fall of the Educated Elite

profiles.name: Thangam Debbonaire
profiles.tagline: House of Lords' Leading Voice on Arts and Culture

profiles.bio:
“In quantum theory, words are blunt tools.” 

Philip Ball is a renowned British science writer and former editor of Nature, celebrated for uncovering the poetic wonder within hard science. In over thirty books — including Critical Mass (Royal Society Winton Prize), Beyond Weird (Physics World Book of the Year), and How Life Works — he explores how science is deeply entwined with culture, politics, and imagination.

From snowflakes and biology to quantum oddities, Ball reveals hidden patterns in nature and challenges the myth of pure objectivity. His work shows how physics sheds light on society, while Beyond Weird invites us to embrace quantum’s counterintuitive logic. His forthcoming book is The Man Who Broke Reality: Niels Bohr and the Making of Modern Physics.

"Ball is a ferociously gifted science writer" — The Sunday Times

events.title: Darwin's Physics and the Evolving Universe

profiles.name: Philip Ball
profiles.tagline: Science Writer Exposing the Limits of Quantum Realism

profiles.bio:
"A failure to understand something does not mean it is irrational. It may simply mean that it lies on the far side of our limited abilities to take things and make complete sense of them."

Alister McGrath holds the Chair in Theology, Ministry and Education at Kings College London, and is Emeritus Andreas Idreos Professor of Science and Religion at Oxford. Beginning his academics in molecular biophysics before turning to Christian theology, McGrath has spent his career arguing that science and faith are not in conflict. 

McGrath is best known for his widely used textbooks Christian Theology: An Introduction and for his robust intellectual challenge to New Atheism, most visibly in The Dawkins Delusion? and The Twilight of Atheism. His prize-winning 2013 biography of C.S. Lewis, which won the ECPA Christian Book Award, confirmed his standing as one of the foremost authorities on Lewis's life and thought. 

"Always highly stimulating" — Tom Holland, co-host of The Rest is History
profiles.name: Alister McGrath
profiles.tagline: Leading Critic of New Atheism

profiles.bio:
"We have known for a long time that antidepressants are not very different from a placebo." 

Professor of Critical and Social Psychiatry at University College London, Joanna Moncrieff is a maverick psychiatrist challenging the multibillion-dollar orthodoxy that depression is caused by a chemical imbalance that can be fixed by medication. In 2022, she led a key study questioning the serotonin theory that underpins much psychiatric treatment.

Moncrieff argues that antidepressants provide only limited benefits, mostly due to placebo effects, while ignoring the complex social and psychological causes of mental illness. Through her books — The Myth of the Chemical Cure, The Bitterest Pill, and Chemically Imbalanced — she exposes the scientific flaws and commercial forces shaping psychiatric care. Her work calls for a more critical, holistic approach to mental health beyond drug treatments.

"[Moncrieff] explains both the scientific flaws and the deliberate manipulations underlying much of today's psychiatric ideology and treatment." — Gabor Maté

events.title: The Misdiagnosed Mind: Depression Through The Ages
Champagne, Cake and Philosophy with Joanna Moncrieff

profiles.name: Joanna Moncrieff
profiles.tagline: Maverick Psychiatrist Exposing the Mental Health Industry

profiles.bio:
"My mental state was a reflection or meditation on my physical state, rather than directly caused by my physical state.”

Edward Bullmore is a neuropsychiatrist, neuroscientist, and academic who has spent much of his career exploring the physical roots of psychiatric conditions. Most notably, his work challenges the traditional divide between body and mind, demonstrating how an overactive immune system and inflammatory biomarkers can be linked to depression and early childhood trauma.

Bullmore has been a Professor of Psychiatry at the University of Cambridge since 1999 and served as the Head of the Department of Psychiatry between 2014 and 2021. He also acts as the Clinical Director of the Behavioural & Clinical Neuroscience Institute. He is the author of several publications, including Fundamentals of Brain Network Analysis and his most popular book, The Inflamed Mind: A Radical New Approach to Depression.

"...one of the world's most accomplished and compassionate psychiatrists." — Karl J. Friston

events.title: Freud, Descartes, and the Matter Behind the Mind

profiles.name: Edward Bullmore
profiles.tagline: Neuroscientist Uncovering the Physical Roots of Depression

profiles.bio:
"It's impossible to think of anything more intrusive or more dangerous or more dystopian."

Silkie Carlo is one of Britain's foremost civil liberties campaigners and the director of Big Brother Watch, the non-party organisation she has led since 2018 in its fight against state surveillance and the erosion of privacy. She has become a familiar face confronting police use of live facial recognition on Britain's streets, and a leading voice against the expansion of the surveillance state, biometric ID, and unchecked data collection.

Before joining Big Brother Watch, Carlo was Senior Advocacy Officer at Liberty, where she led work on technology and human rights and launched a legal challenge to the Investigatory Powers Act. She previously worked on Edward Snowden's official defence fund and has campaigned for whistleblowers at risk. She is the co-author of Information Security for Journalists, and writes regularly in the Telegraph, Guardian, and Mail.

"A passionate campaigner for the protection of liberties" ― Institute of Advanced Legal Studies

events.title: The Nation State vs Big Tech

profiles.name: Silkie Carlo
profiles.tagline: Britain's Leading Critic of the Surveillance State

profiles.bio:
"I look at the history of physics and I see how we've been in similar situations before... I believe there is a real world, and we need to find out about it."

Antony Valentini is a theoretical physicist and author tackling the most foundational issues in quantum mechanics. He has held research positions at the University of Rome La Sapienza, Imperial College London, and Perimeter Institute for Theoretical Physics. He is currently academic visitor at Imperial College London.

Valentini is the co-author of Quantum Theory at the Crossroads, which explores the development of quantum theory at the time of the Fifth Solvay Conference. His most recent book Beyond the Quantum: A Quest for the Origin and Hidden Meaning of Quantum Mechanics offers a comprehensive rethink of quantum mechanics.

"Valentini stands as the most important thinker of this century defending the notion that science gives a complete description of physical processes." — Lee Smolin
profiles.name: Antony Valentini
profiles.tagline: Quantum Theory's Most Formidable Realist

profiles.bio:
"The geometry, the content, and the fate of the universe are all intricately linked."

Priyamvada Natarajan is an award-winning theoretical astrophysicist known for her work in mapping dark matter and dark energy through gravitational lensing. She is an astronomy and physics professor at Yale University, and the author of the bestseller Mapping the Heavens — The Radical Scientific Ideas That Reveal the Cosmos.

Natarajan was included in the TIME 100 list of most influential people in the world in 2024 for her path-breaking contributions to Astrophysics.

“A strikingly lucid account of the expansion, not just of the universe, but of the way we have tried to understand it." — New York Times
profiles.name: Priya Natarajan
profiles.tagline: Astrophysicist in TIME Magazine's 100 Most Influential People

profiles.bio:
"In order to change the system, we need to change our ideas."

Martin Wolf is the chief economics commentator of the Financial Times and is widely regarded as the most connected financial journalist in the world. He is a visiting fellow at Nuffield college Oxford, Special professor at the University of Nottingham, and fellow of the World Economic Forum. 

Martin Wolf's journalism has been credited with the "Keynesian Resurgence" seen throughout the West in the wake of the financial crisis. His most recent book The Crisis of Democratic Capitalism is the culmination of a lifetime at the forefront of economic analysis, and sets out a bold vision to fix the drift between Capitalism and Democracy.

"He really is the premier financial and economics writer in the world" — Kenneth Rogoff

events.title: The Future of the AI Economy

profiles.name: Martin Wolf
profiles.tagline: Chief Economics Commentator at the Financial Times

profiles.bio:
"If all narratives are relative, then we are lost."

David Aaronovitch is an award-winning journalist and presenter on BBC Radio 4's Briefing Room, who previously wrote a column in The Times for nearly two decades. A rigorous, evidence-based myth-buster, he has spent his career puncturing conspiracy theories and challenging received wisdom.

Aaronovitch is the author of Voodoo Histories: The Role of Conspiracy Theory in Shaping Modern History, exposing how conspiracies gain support and fuel violence. His other books include Paddling to Jerusalem: An Aquatic Tour of Our Small Country and most recently a memoir about his family and early life, Party Animals: My Family and Other Communists. He now writes Notes From the Underground on Substack, where he continues to sift through our modern political myths and crises.

“An effervescent and essential writer.” — The Observer
profiles.name: David Aaronovitch
profiles.tagline: Journalist Who Predicted Our Age of Conspiracies

profiles.bio:
"If you don't read Aristotle in Greek, you cannot understand his argument."

Babette Babich is a world-leading expert on Nietzsche and a fearless defender of continental philosophy. Professor of philosophy at Fordham University and editor of the journal New Nietzsche Studies, Babich has spent decades dismantling common assumptions about science, art, and the nature of knowledge itself.

Educated in both the analytic and continental traditions, Babich has written extensively on figures like Adorno, Gadamer, and Foucault, challenging the boundaries between art, science, and philosophy. Her latest book, titled Ivan Illich's Philosophical Constellations, examines the thought of the Austrian cultural critic and polymath — specifically, his radical critique of modern institutions.
 
"[Babich] succeeds in penetrating the cloud of suspicion, incomprehension, and distrust that for contemporary readers surrounds Nietzsche's writing." — New Nietzsche Studies

events.title: Heidegger, Rilke, and the Limits of Language

profiles.name: Babette Babich
profiles.tagline: Defender of Continental Philosophy

profiles.bio:
"Experts may be the most likely source of incremental advances, but radical rethinks tend to come from outsiders."

Sebastian Mallaby is a journalist and author widely regarded as one of the world's leading commentators on global finance, economic policy, and the forces reshaping capitalism. A two-time Pulitzer Prize finalist, he is the Paul A. Volcker Senior Fellow for International Economics at the Council on Foreign Relations and a longtime columnist for The Washington Post. Before that, he spent thirteen years at The Economist — reporting from Africa, Japan, and Washington — building a reputation for making complex systems legible and consequential.

He is the author of several acclaimed books, including More Money Than God, The Man Who Knew, and The Power Law. His most recent book, The Infinity Machine: Demis Hassabis, DeepMind and the Quest for Superintelligence, is a New York Times and Sunday Times bestseller — and the product of rare, privileged access to the founder and inner workings of the world's most consequential AI laboratory.

"Thoroughly magnificent" — John Tammy, Forbes

events.title: The Future of the AI Economy
The Nation State vs Big Tech

profiles.name: Sebastian Mallaby
profiles.tagline: Journalist Demystifying the World of AI

profiles.bio:
"Putin has banned me from Russia. It’s a badge of pride."

Malcolm Rifkind is one of Britain's most experienced foreign policy voices.
