He served as both Foreign Secretary and Defence Secretary under Margaret Thatcher and John Major, spanning two full prime ministerships, and went on to chair the Intelligence and Security Committee, overseeing the work of MI5, MI6, and GCHQ. 

In 1997, he was knighted in recognition of his public service. He has been highly critical of Russia's invasion of Ukraine and has advocated that Britain expand its own military. 

"Malcolm Rifkind was in the top rank of twentieth-century politicians. Few saw events at closer quarters" — John Major

events.title: Winning and Losing on the Global Stage

profiles.name: Malcolm Rifkind
profiles.tagline: Britain's Veteran Foreign Policy Voice

profiles.bio:
“Psychological phenomena cannot be reduced to physiological ones any more than lightning can be reduced to thunder."

Mark Solms is a psychoanalyst, renowned for discovering the brain mechanisms of dreaming and founding the field of neuropsychoanalysis. Where mainstream neuroscience abandoned the mind in favour of the brain, Solms has spent his career insisting they cannot be separated, rehabilitating Freud's deepest insights and grounding them in 21st-century science. He holds the Chair of Neuropsychology at the University of Cape Town and Groote Schuur Hospital, and serves as the President of the South African Psychoanalytical Association.

Solms is the author of The Brain and the Inner World, a bestseller translated into 13 languages, and The Hidden Spring: A Journey to the Source of Consciousness. His forthcoming work, The Only Cure, seeks to rehabilitate the legacy of pyschoanalysis for a 21st-century audience. 

"It would be difficult to improve on Solms's credentials for the task he sets himself" — Raymond Tallis, The Guardian

events.title: Freud, Descartes, and the Matter Behind the Mind
Champagne, Cake and Philosophy with Mark Solms

profiles.name: Mark Solms
profiles.tagline: Neuroscientist Who Discovered Why We Dream

profiles.bio:
"I care about good people who live virtuous lives, who engage in the world — who are rational."

Yaron Brook is an Israeli-American entrepreneur, writer, activist, and political scientist. He is currently chairman of the board of the Ayn Rand Institute where he can be heard weekly on The Yaron Brook Show, which airs live on the BlogTalkRadio podcast. He is also a frequent guest on national radio and television programs including C-SPAN and CNBC.  

Brook is coauthor, with Don Watkins, of the national best-seller Free Market Revolution: How Ayn Rand's Ideas Can End Big Government and Equal Is Unfair: America's Misguided Fight Against Income Inequality.

"At LAST the voice of reason breaks through the prejudices and presumptions and outright misrepresentations." — Mark Pellegrino
profiles.name: Yaron Brook
profiles.tagline: Radical for Capitalism

profiles.bio:
“The worship of safety represents a profoundly pessimistic attitude towards human potential.”

Frank Furedi is a trailblazing sociologist and social commentator. He currently serves as emeritus professor of sociology at the University of Kent, where his work on fear, education, and therapy culture has made him one of the most widely cited sociologists of the 21st century.

His recent books cover the culture wars, democracy, borders, and fear as broad topics. The through line of his work is an analysis of how Western democracies fail to account for risk and uncertainty in decision-making. 

"Professor Furedi has written an important book ... which is essential to the understanding of our times."  — Theodore Dalrymple, Sunday Telegraph

events.title: The History and Philosophy of Populism
In Search of the Grown Up
Danger and Risk in an Anxious World

profiles.name: Frank Furedi
profiles.tagline: Leading Sociologist Who Predicted the Culture Wars

profiles.bio:
"The hunger for ‘content’ is keeping us culturally stuck."

Jemima Kelly is a columnist and journalist at the Financial Times, where she writes on society, politics, and ideas, ranging from culture wars to crypto. Alongside her column she writes long reads, travel pieces and other features as well as a quarterly column for HTSI called “Adventures in Woo Woo." 

She previously worked as a reporter at Reuters from 2013 to 2018, before joining the FT, where she first made her name at FT Alphaville, the paper's markets and finance blog.

"One of the most original and interesting voices in the British press." — Ian Leslie

events.title: In Search of the Grown Up
Champagne, Cake and Philosophy with Jemima Kelly

profiles.name: Jemima Kelly
profiles.tagline: Financial Times Columnist

profiles.bio:
"The age of labour, where paid work is the foundation of society, will no longer be viable."

Daniel Susskind is a leading economist on technology, automation, and the future of work. He is the Mercers' School Memorial Professor of Business at Gresham College, a Research Professor at King's College London, a Senior Research Associate at the Institute for Ethics in AI at Oxford, and a Digital Fellow at the Stanford Digital Economy Lab. He also sits on the UK Government's Expert Panel on AI and the Future of Work.

Susskind is the bestselling author of A World Without Work and Growth: A Reckoning, chosen by President Obama as one of his favourite books of 2024. His new book, What Should My Children Do? How To Flourish in the Age of AI, publishes this September and asks how the next generation should prepare for a world transformed by artificial intelligence.

"A tour de force." — Gordon Brown

events.title: The Rise and Fall of the Educated Elite
Rethinking Education in the Age of AI

profiles.name: Daniel Susskind
profiles.tagline: Leading Voice on AI and the Future of Work

profiles.bio:
"The economy, like science or art, is more like an organism growing uncertainly toward the light than a steel machine repeating exactly today and tomorrow what it did yesterday."

Deirdre McCloskey is an American economist, historian, and rhetorician, trained at Harvard University. Distinguished Professor Emerita of Economics, History and English at the University of Illinois, Chicago, McCloskey has written twenty-five books and over 400 scholarly pieces. Her "humanomics" remains one of the most contested and consequential theses in contemporary economic thought. 

McCloskey's Bourgeois trilogy — The Bourgeois Virtues, Bourgeois Dignity, and Bourgeois Equality — won the Manhattan Institute's Hayek Book Prize. She has also received the Adam Smith Prize, the Hayek Lifetime Achievement Award, and the Julian Simon Prize. Now, current holder of the Isaiah Berlin Chair in Liberal Thought at the Cato Institute, McCloskey remains one of the most provocative and wide-ranging voices in economics today. 

"[B]racingly well-informed and original " — Matt Ridley

events.title: Hollywood, Hegel and the Myth of the Good

profiles.name: Deirdre McCloskey
profiles.tagline: Economist Rewriting the Story of Capitalism

profiles.bio:
"The best way to stop girls achieving anything is to force them to achieve everything."

Laurie Penny is a journalist, author, and screenwriter whose writing on feminism, power, and politics has made them one of the most distinctive and provocative voices on the British left. Penny is a contributing editor at the New Statesman and regular contributor to The Guardian, The Spectator, and The New York Times.

Penny is the author of seven books, including Sexual Revolution: Modern Fascism and the Feminist Fightback, Cybersexism: Sex, Gender and Power on the Internet, and Bitch Doctrine: Essays for Dissenting Adults, which was longlisted for the 2018 Orwell Prize. Their blog Penny Red, launched in 2007, was shortlisted for the Orwell Prize for blogging in 2010. As a screenwriter, Penny has worked for HBO, Netflix, and Amazon, with credits including The Haunting of Bly Manor and The Nevers.

"Brilliant; vital; revolutionary" — Kate Manne

events.title: In Search of the Grown Up

profiles.name: Laurie Penny
profiles.tagline: Provocative Voice on Gender and Power

profiles.bio:
"I think it's reasonable to suppose that one could oscillate between being biologically 20 and biologically 25 indefinitely.”

Aubrey de Grey is a pioneer of longevity science and a biomedical gerontologist whose work has transformed the debate around human ageing. Best known as the founder of the SENS (Strategies for Engineered Negligible Senescence) approach to rejuvenation biotechnology, he is currently President and Chief Science Officer of the Longevity Escape Velocity Foundation, where he leads research aimed at preventing and reversing age-related damage. 

He is the author of the books Ending Ageing and The Mitochondrial Free Radical Theory of Ageing. Admired by supporters as a visionary and criticised by sceptics as overly ambitious, he has forced scientists, philosophers, and policymakers alike to confront one of humanity's oldest questions: must we grow old?

"There's something of the Old Testament prophet about Aubrey de Grey." — The Guardian
profiles.name: Aubrey de Grey
profiles.tagline: Thinker Behind Longevity Escape Velocity

profiles.bio:
“Given the amount of suffering and injustice in the world, I flip-flop between thinking that doing philosophy is a complete luxury and that it is an absolute necessity."

Sally Haslanger is the Ford Professor of Philosophy at MIT and a philosopher of gender and race. Having earned her PhD from the University of California, Berkeley, and taught at Princeton, Haslanger is recognised as one of the foremost analytic feminists in the US. 

Haslanger's book Resisting Reality: Social Construction and Social Critique was awarded the Joseph B. Gittler Prize in 2014 for "outstanding scholarly contribution in the field of the philosophy." Her recent work Ideology in Practice: What Does Ideology Do? explores how systematic structures shape identity and inequality. 

"Outstanding scholarly contributon in the field of philosophy of one or more of the social sciences" — Joseh B Gittler Prize, 2014

events.title: Gender, Race, and the Structures of Power
Reality in the Age of Perspective

profiles.name: Sally Haslanger
profiles.tagline: Pioneer of Feminist Social Theory

profiles.bio:
"Science differs from politics only in that the masks of its players rarely drop."

Steve Fuller is a professor of sociology at the University of Warwick. He is the founder of the research program of social epistemology. It is the name of a quarterly journal he founded with Taylor & Francis in 1987, as well as the first of his twenty-five books. 

Fuller is renowned for his work on the post-truth condition, which inspired his 2018 book Post-Truth: Knowledge as a Power Game. His other books include Humanity 2.0, Kuhn vs Popper, and Back to the University's Future, and his most recent book is Media and the Power of Knowledge.

"Fuller is a tall and invariably animated figure." ― The Guardian

events.title: Reality in the Age of Perspective

profiles.name: Steve Fuller
profiles.tagline: Renegade Post-Truth Philosopher

profiles.bio:
"Science is not a list of facts. It’s a process, and the first step in that process is to embrace what we don’t know.”

Daniel  Whiteson is an experimental particle physicist and professor of Physics and Astronomy at University of California, Irvine, whose work explores the deepest mysteries of matter, energy, and the unknown universe. He has worked at CERN's Large Hadron Collider on the ATLAS experiment and is a fellow of the American Physical Society. 

Whiteson is the co-author, with Jorge Cham, of We Have No Idea: A Guide to the Unknown Universe and Frequently Asked Questions About the Universe. Together they also host the podcast Daniel and Jorge Explain the Universe. Whiteson's most recent book Do Aliens Speak Physics? asks if the common idea that maths and physics are a universal language is really true.

"Reveals the humbling vastness of our ignorance about the universe" — Carlo Rovelli

events.title: Darwin's Physics and the Evolving Universe
Alien Minds and the Universality of Physics

profiles.name: Daniel Whiteson
profiles.tagline: Physicist Exposing Unanswered Questions of the Universe

profiles.bio:
"It seems to me that if were we all equally obsessed with our bodies, this would not be a good world to live in at all. It would not be a world of human flourishing."

Heather Widdows is a leading philosopher of applied and global ethics, whose work has forced both academia and popular culture to confront the ethical dimensions of beauty, identity, and the body. Currently Professor of Philosophy at the University of Warwick, she previously served as Pro-Vice-Chancellor for Research at the University of Birmingham, where she held the prestigious John Ferguson Chair of Global Ethics.

Her most recent book Perfect Me: Beauty as an Ethical Ideal argues that the pressure to attain physical perfection has moved beyond vanity — it has become a dominant moral framework shaping how women understand their own worth and failure. Her other major works include Global Ethics and The Connected Self: The Ethics and Governance of the Genetic Individual.

"Innovative and original." — Anne Phillips
profiles.name: Heather Widdows
profiles.tagline: Philosopher Exposing the Moral Tyranny of Beauty

profiles.bio:
"Even in an era of open data, data science and data journalism, we still need basic statistical principles in order not to be misled by apparent patterns in the numbers."

David Spiegelhalter is an Emeritus professor of Statistics at the University of Cambridge and formerly the Chair of the Winton Centre for Risk and Evidence Communication. A world-renowned statistician and best-selling author, he has done pioneering work on improving the way statistical evidence is used by policy-makers, legal personnel and healthcare professionals, especially during the Covid-19 pandemic. In 2014, he was knighted for his services to the field of medical statistics.

He is a prominent media personality alongside his academic work, having presented the BBC4 documentaries “Tails you Win: the Science of Chance” and the award-winning “Climate Change by Numbers. His latest book The Art of Uncertainty: How to Navigate Chance, Ignorence, Risk and Luck published in eleven languages, questions the role luck and chance play in our lives.

"David Spiegelhalter is probably the greatest living statistical communicator; more than that, he's one of the great communicators in any field" — Tim Harford.

events.title: Danger and Risk in an Anxious World

profiles.name: David Spiegelhalter
profiles.tagline: Leading Authority on Risk and Statistics

profiles.bio:
"In jail, philosophy comes from the ground up, not the top down."

Andy West is the author of The Life Inside: A Memoir of Prison, Family and Learning to be Free and the Executive Producer of the acclaimed BBC adaptation of that book Waiting for the Out. The book and TV show feature the conversations he has with people in prison about their lives, discussing their ideas and working to disciover new ways to think about their situation. The Life Inside was an Irish Times and The i Book of the Year

He has written for 3AM, the Guardian, The Times Education Supplement, The Millions, Litro, Boundless and Bloomsbury. 

“An authentic, fascinating and deeply moving story about the different ways people search for freedom.” — Terry Waite
profiles.name: Andy West
profiles.tagline: BBC Drama Author Exploring the Nature of Freedom

profiles.bio:
"If you hack the code of reality... you control the universe."

Melvin Vopson is a physicist and leading proponent of the view that the universe is fundamentally made of information. Associate Professor of Physics at the University of Portsmouth and Founder and CEO of the Information Physics Institute, Vopson has spent his career exploring the ultimate nature of reality.

His mass-energy-information equivalence principle and his second law of infodynamics have attracted international attention for their radical implications. Where the second law of thermodynamics tells us entropy in physical systems increases over time, Vopson found that entropy in information systems remains constant or falls — a finding with profound consequences for genetics, evolution, and our understanding of reality itself. He is also the author of Reality Reloaded: The Scientific Case for a Simulated Universe.

"Wide-ranging scientific expertise in experimental, applied and theoretical physics that is internationally recognized." — The Creative Process
profiles.name: Melvin Vopson
profiles.tagline: Physicist Making Scientific Case for a Simulated Universe

profiles.bio:
"Love can seem like an attempt to give to somebody what we don't quite have (to make them happy) and ending up giving them something they don't quite want."

Dr Agnieszka Piotrowska is a multi award-winning filmmaker, psychologist, and writer whose work explores desire, intimacy and the stories we tell about our relationships with others, ourselves and, increasingly, intelligent machines. Her films and research have taken her across Europe, Africa and North America. In Zimbabwe, she explored desire and relationships across ethnic divisions and social prohibitions, while her documentary Married to the Eiffel Tower examined objectum sexuality and the nature of human attachment long before questions of AI intimacy entered public debate.

Agnieszka is the author of AI Intimacy and Psychoanalysis (Routledge, 2026), one of the first books to examine the psychological and emotional dimensions of relationships with artificial intelligence. Her work brings together psychoanalysis, philosophy, cinema and emerging technology to ask what AI reveals about our deepest desires for recognition, connection and understanding.

“Formidably interesting… truly engaged and engaging.” —  Alenka Zupančič
profiles.name: Agnieszka Piotrowska
profiles.tagline: Psychologist and Author Rewriting the Rules of Desire

profiles.bio:
"The right wing has powerful contagious moods that help spread their ideas."

Tony D. Sampson is an academic author whose research connects digital culture, media theory, and political philosophy. He is a Reader in Digital Communication at the University of Essex Business School and co-founder of the Cultural Engine Research Group. Author of several books including Virality, A Sleepwalker’s Guide to Social Media, and The Assemblage Brain, his work examines how networked media environments shape behaviour, attention, and political life.

He is due to publish a new book early in spring 2027 with the University of Minnesota Press titled Birth, School, Work, Death: UX and the Struggle Against Life-Cycle Optimization. The project extends his analysis of digital influence by examining how the logic of user experience design increasingly structures institutions and everyday practices across the life course.

"Impressive and ambitious" — Brian Rotman

events.title: Life, the Self, and the Infinite Scroll

profiles.name: Tony D. Sampson
profiles.tagline: Digital Contagion Theorist

profiles.bio:
"The future is made by the things we imagine today."

Güneş Taylor is a molecular biologist and Chancellor's Fellow at the University of Edinburgh's Centre for Reproductive Health, where her research focuses on the genetic formation of ovaries and testes and the molecular basis of fertility and menopause. Trained at Oxford and the Francis Crick Institute, she brings a working scientist's precision to questions usually left to philosophers and pundits — genome editing, sex differences, and the future of reproduction.

Both "an incredible science communicator" and a scientist herself, she has become a distinguished HowtheLightGetsIn host, sharing the stage with Slavoj Zizek, Richard Dawkins, Yuval Noah Harari, and more. In 2018, Güneş was awarded the Crick Public Engagement Prize for her efforts in the public communication of science.

"Güneş has performed a significant service to disseminating the work within her field." — Anastasia de Waal
profiles.name: Güneş Taylor
profiles.tagline: Award-Winning Geneticist and Science Communicator

profiles.bio:
"I love philosophy but it shouldn’t be just for the elite. We should all be asking these questions.”

Joanna Kavenna is an award-winning writer. A seasoned traveler, she was born in the UK, but has lived in the US, France, Germany, Scandinavia and the Baltic states. Her travels led to her first book, The Ice Museum, which details her experience traveling in the remote North. In 2013 she was named as one of Granta’s Best Young British Novelists.

Her latest book, Seven, is described as an absurdist, philosophical novel and explores the dystopian reality of big-tech and the digital meshing of humanity and technology.

"Wonderful, impossible, dynamic" — Observer

events.title: The End of the Book: A Civilisation in Crisis

profiles.name: Joanna Kavenna
profiles.tagline: Award-Winning Novelist

profiles.bio:
"It's hard to have a settled view about America, and maybe it's actually unhelpful."

John Prideaux is Executive Editor at The Economist, writing as one of the most authoritative voices on American politics and global affairs today. With a formidable background writing for the Financial Times and New Statesman,researching in the House of Commons and European Parliament, Prideaux has reported extensively across the UK, US, India and Brazil. 

Prideaux built and ran The Economist's award-winning podcast department, including the flagship politics podcast Checks and Balance. A regular analyst on BBC News, CNN, Fox News, Sky News and NPR, he has covered some of the most consequential political moments of the last two decades. 

"Prideaux became one of [The Economist's] most prominent interpreters of American politics and culture" - Forbes

events.title: Winning and Losing on the Global Stage

profiles.name: John Prideaux
profiles.tagline: Executive Editor of The Economist

profiles.bio:
"The analysis that is informing government planning is a step behind how fast climate change and then its supercharging of disasters is. And that should be a moment of profound alarm"

Laurie Laybourn is an award-winning researcher, author and strategist whose work sits at the intersection of climate risk, public policy and system change. Executive director of the Strategic Climate Risks Initiative (SCRI), he is an Associate Fellow at Chatham House and holds fellowships at the Institute for Public Policy Research and the Global Systems Institute, University of Exeter. 

Drawing on experience across academia, activism, and policymaking, including previous roles at the LSE, Oxford University, and the UK Parliament, Laybourn has become one of the most compelling voices on the consequences of climate change.

"This book sets out the scale of the emergency as well as marks out the route to a better society. This is an essential read." — John McDonnell, MP, on Laybourn's book Planet on Fire: A Manifesto for the Age of Environmental Breakdown

events.title: Breaking Free of the Doom Loop

profiles.name: Laurie Laybourn
profiles.tagline: Pre-eminent climate action strategist

profiles.bio:
"The nation-state system [...] is not capable, even in theory, of protecting populations from twenty-first-century conditions"

Rana Dasgupta is a novelist and essayist. A visiting fellow in the humanities at Princeton and lecturer at Brown University, he has built a reputation as one of the sharpest critical voices on globalisation, migration, and the modern city. 

In 2010, The Daily Telegraph named him one of Britain's best novelists under 40; in 2014 Le Monde listed him among 70 people shaping the world tomorrow. Dasgupta was also awarded the prestigious Windham-Campbell Prize for Nonfiction in 2025. His most recent book, After Nations: The Making and Unmaking of a World Order, continues his rigorous reputation with a historical and philosophical reckoning. 

"Simply astonishing […] Dasgupta is consistently insightful, thought-provoking, and on point." - David Wengrow

events.title: Breaking Free of the Doom Loop

profiles.name: Rana Dasgupta
profiles.tagline: Global storyteller mapping the tremors of globalisation

profiles.bio:
"Clothes tell our stories, some that we would rather not tell, others that we hardly know ourselves"

Shahidha Bari is a critic, academic, and broadcaster whose work spans literature, philosophy, fashion, and the history of ideas. Professor of Fashion Cultures and Histories at the London College of Fashion, University of the Arts London, she has built a reputation as one of Britain's most wide-ranging and intellectually ambitious cultural voices. 

Her book Dressed: A Philosophy of Clothes reads fashion not as vanity but as a key to understanding identity, desire, and what it means to be human. Her most recent book, Look Again: Fashion argues that thinking seriously about dress takes us into the heart of society, culture, and politics. Bari is also a host of BBC Radio 4's arts and ideas programme Free Thinking.

"A deeply original, compelling thinker and a brilliant writer." ― Simon Critchley
profiles.name: Shahidha Bari
profiles.tagline: Cultural Critic and Champion of the Humanities

profiles.bio:
"We never solve problems by denying our disruptive power. We solve problems by embracing that."

Jay Shapiro is an award-winning filmmaker, writer, and podcaster. Director of Islam and the Future of Tolerance, a documentary based on the provocative dialogue between Sam Harris and Maajid Nawaz, Shapiro consistently tackles complex themes in films such as Opposite Field, All Rise, and Metamorphosis. 

From his blog, What Jay Thinks, to his Dilemma podcast, which includes co-hosted episodes with public intellectuals like Coleman Hughes, Shapiro brings a philosophical edge to everything he creates. Shapiro uses film, conversation, and criticism to ask hard questions about identity, values, and collective future, making him a uniquely relevant voice in today's discourse.

events.title: The Code for Good and Evil
Life, the Self, and the Infinite Scroll
Danger and Risk in an Anxious World

profiles.name: Jay Shapiro
profiles.tagline: Documentary filmmaker probing the moral dilemmas of our time

profiles.bio:
"Men are assumed to be competent until proven otherwise, whereas a woman is assumed to be incompetent until she proves otherwise.”

Mary Ann Sieghart is a journalist, author, and public intellectual committed to dismantling the invisible yet powerful bias she calls “the authority gap.” A former Assistant Editor at The Times and BBC presenter, Sieghart now leads The Authority Gap Consultancy and serves as Visiting Professor at King’s College London, challenging societal norms about gender, credibility, and leadership.

Her breakthrough book, The Authority Gap: Why Women Are Still Taken Less Seriously Than Men, and What We Can Do About It, combines rigorous research with real-world stories—including voices like Baroness Hale and Mary Beard—to expose how women remain under‑validated despite equal or superior expertise. A prominent voice in media and policy, she has chaired the Social Market Foundation, judged the Women’s Prize for Fiction, and is a trustee of high-profile organizations.

“Deeply researched, profoundly thoughtful and a book very much for the here and now...” — Andrew Marr, on The Authority Gap

events.title: The Life and Philosophy of Michael Gove

profiles.name: Mary Ann Sieghart
profiles.tagline: Pioneer of the "Authority Gap"

profiles.bio:
"Philosophy isn’t a subject you study; it’s a way of seeing the world differently.”

Jonny Thomson is a British philosopher, teacher, and writer whose work brings the history of ideas to a broad, modern audience. Before becoming a full-time writer, Thomson spent years teaching philosophy in Oxford, where he developed a reputation for making complex thinkers relevant to everyday life. He is a columnist at Big Think, where his widely read philosophy essays introduce classic ideas through contemporary examples.

Thomson is the author of Mini Philosophy: A Small Book of Big Ideas, a concise guide to some of the most influential thinkers and concepts in the history of philosophy. He is also the founder of Mini Philosophy's social network, explaining philosophical ideas to an audience of over two million.

""Engaging, smart, and wise."" — David Mitchell"

events.title: In Search of the Grown Up

profiles.name: Jonny Thomson
profiles.tagline: Founder of Mini Philosophy

profiles.bio:
"There is a serious prospect that, in our time, we are losing faith in politics. The words of politicians float by, practised and polished, but profligate."
Philip Collins is the Editor of Prospect magazine, Founder and CEO of The Draft, and visiting fellow at the London School of Economics. He was previosly contributing editor at The New Statesman, a columnist for the Evening Standard, and the former lead writer at The Times.

Having previously been lead speech writer for Tony Blair, the Director of the Social Market Foundation think tank and an Equity Strategist at two investment banks, Collins' wealth of experience makes him a trusted voice in the political fray.

"Phil Collins is the best political commentator in Britain." ― Michael Burleigh
profiles.name: Phil Collins
profiles.tagline: The Wordsmith Who Shapes Public Debate

profiles.bio:
Danielle Sands is a philosopher, writer, and senior lecturer at Royal Holloway, University of London, whose work spans literature, philosophy, and critical theory. With a rare ability to move between classic texts and contemporary culture, Sands explores how philosophy can shed light on modern moral and political landscapes.

Sands is best known for her work on continental philosophy, drawing on thinkers from Derrida to Spinoza to reframe how we understand belief in the age of disillusionment. She is the author of Animal Writing: Storytelling, Selfhood and the Limits of Empathy and, most recently, Writing Religion & Politics After Derrida.

"Bold, provocative and highly enjoyable." — Rosi Braidotti
profiles.name: Danielle Sands
profiles.tagline: Philosopher of the Anthropocene

profiles.bio:
"Don’t argue about how much salt there is in food — this can save relationships — you live in different taste worlds; you’ve got different taste buds.”

Barry Smith is Director of the Institute of Philosophy at the University of London's School of Advanced Study and co-director of the Centre for the Study of the Senses. In 2010, he made waves with his insightful BBC World Service series ""The Mysteries of the Brain.""

Barry also harbours a deep passion for wine, often hosting engaging wine-tasting events at festivals. He incorporates his studies on the multisensory nature of experience into these sessions, creating a unique, fascinating blend. Barry also lends his wine expertise to The World of Fine Wine and Prospect Magazine as a regular contributor and wine columnist.

“Well up to the task of situating wine-centered questions within a larger framework of questions about taste and perception, subjectivity and objectivity.” — The TLS

events.title: Wine Tasting and Philosophy with Barry C. Smith
Whisky Tasting and Philosophy with Barry C. Smith

profiles.name: Barry C Smith
profiles.tagline: Philosopher putting the senses under the microscope

profiles.bio:
"Cosmology looks rather like a historical accident of ideas... overdetermined by the implications of its past inventions.”

Bjørn Ekeberg is a Norwegian philosopher of science, author, entrepreneur, and cultural creator whose work challenges orthodox thinking in cosmology, scientific knowledge, and human understanding. He holds a Ph.D. in philosophy of science from the University of Victoria (Canada) and has combined rigorous academic inquiry with creative and practical ventures.

Ekeberg’s philosophical writing spans cosmology, metaphysics, and the limits of scientific knowledge, exemplified by his book Metaphysical Experiments: Physics and the Invention of the Universe, which critiques assumptions in modern physics and invites fresh perspectives on how we understand the universe. 

"Makes a radical case that will interest philosophers of science and contemplative scientists alike.” — Brian Rotman
profiles.name: Bjørn Ekeberg
profiles.tagline: Philosopher of Science Challenging Our Understanding of Reality

profiles.bio:
"If it is there, if it is a story, we put it out there."

Roger Hearing is a veteran journalist and broadcaster. Over a 35-year career with the BBC and Bloomberg, he has covered wars, elections, coups and revolutions across the globe ― including the UN intervention in Somalia and the Rwandan genocide.

From 1999 to 2010, he presented The World Today and News Hour for the BBC World Service, along with the World Tonight on BBC Radio 4. He now co-hosts the podcast The Why? Curve with Phil Dobbie.

"An excellent thoughtful broadcaster and a rock solid journalist." ― Ian D. Richardson, former editor at BBC World Service
profiles.name: Roger Hearing
profiles.tagline: Veteran Journalist and Presenter

profiles.bio:
"My idea of hell would be to live somewhere comfortable where no one ever talked about anything serious."

Isabel Hilton is a journalist, broadcaster and expert on all things international relations. Hilton boasts a highly accomplished career in national and international media, having reported from China, South Asia, Latin America, Africa and the Middle East for the BBC, The Sunday Times, the Independent, and the Guardian. 
 
Hilton is a particularly formidable authority on China. In 2006, she founded Chinadialogue, a fully bilingual not-for-profit newsroom dedicated to sparking intelligent discourse and fostering a global understanding of China's environmental challenges. 

"Lively and vastly entertaining..." — Boston Sunday Globe
profiles.name: Isabel Hilton
profiles.tagline: Leading Voice Bridging China and the West

profiles.bio:
Robin Clyfan is an award-winning comedian, interviewer, and host. From Oxford and Cambridge to the Tate Modern, he has a rare ability to create an atmosphere that is simultaneously rigorous and joyful, bringing comedic instinct and intellectual curiosity to the biggest questions in philosophy, science, and culture. 

Clyfan is the host and producer of Thinking Deeply, a series developed with Oxford University's Wadham College and The Ned London, in which he interviews leading figures from across the worlds of science, politics, and ideas — recent guests include Christopher Summerfield, Research Director of the UK AI Safety Institute. 

"one of the best MCs in the business." — BBC Radio 4
profiles.name: Robin Clyfan
profiles.tagline: Award-Winning Comedian and Intellectual Provocateur

profiles.bio:
"The status of philosophy is such that it is not the case that you cannot be wrong in philosophy but that it is very difficult to be right."

Peter Worley is the founder and former CEO of The Philosophy Foundation, a pioneering charity that has spent over two decades bringing philosophy into schools, prisons, care homes, and communities across Britain. A philosopher, educator, and author, Worley developed the Philosophy in Education Project and the PhiE method — an accessible approach to doing philosophy with children that has influenced educators across the world.

Worley is the author of numerous books, including The If Machine and 40 Lessons to Get Children Thinking. His work was the basis for a BAFTA-nominated BBC series What Makes Me, Me?

"stimulating and imaginative" — Nigel Warburton
profiles.name: Peter Worley
profiles.tagline: Founder and former CEO of The Philosophy Foundation

profiles.bio:
"I think that philosophy offers a way for adults to reconnect with this childlike openness to possibility."

Steven Campbell-Harris is a Senior Specialist and Teacher Trainer at The Philosophy Foundation, an award-winning charity that brings philosophy into schools and the wider community. He has spent years working directly with children, teachers, and institutions to embed rigorous philosophical thinking in educational settings — training the next generation of philosophy educators and demonstrating, classroom by classroom, that big questions are for everyone.

Alongside his work in schools, Campbell-Harris writes A Question Of…, a new series for the Philosophers' Magazine that introduces philosophy to young readers.
profiles.name: Steven Campbell-Harris
profiles.tagline: Champion of Philosophy for the Next Generation

profiles.bio:
"We still believe that ideas matter."

WANG Hui is the Distinguished Professor in the School of Humanities at Tsinghua University and Director of the Tsinghua Institute for Advanced Study in the Humanities and Social Sciences. He has been elected as a foreign member of Academia Europaea (MAE) since 2024. His research interests include Chinese intellectual history, Chinese literature and social and political theory.
He has received numerous awards for his scholarship, including the Luca Pacioli Award (2013), Anneliese Maier Research Award(2018) and Antonio Feltrinelli International Prize (2026), and has been Visiting Professor and fellow at Harvard, Edinburgh, Bologna, Stanford, UCLA, Berkeley, Tokyo University,the University of Washington, Wissenschaft Kolleg zu Berlin and Swedish Collegium for Advanced Study among others. His recent English publications include The Rise of Modern Chinese Thought (2022), China’s Twentieth Century (2016), China from Empire to Nation-State (2015), and The Politics of Imagining Asia (2011).

"He is, deservedly, the best-known intellectual associated with China's New Left." — Kaiser Kuo

events.title: China, the West, and the Myth of Modernity
Hollywood, Hegel and the Myth of the Good

profiles.name: Wang Hui
profiles.tagline: Leading Voice of the Chinese New Left

profiles.bio:
"Because philosophy starts with questions it carries with it a sense of amazement at the world, at language, at our own selves and at others."

Maria Balaska is a philosopher whose work brings together continental philosophy, ethics, psychoanalysis, and political thought. She is a non-residential research fellow in Philosophy at Åbo Akademi University, where her research explores subjectivity, language, critique, and the limits of experience.

Her more recent work turns to the ethical and existential stakes of experience itself. In Anxiety & Wonder: On Being Human, she explores how moods without clear objects can disclose the groundlessness and creativity of human sense-making. Maria has written for the Los Angeles Review of Books, Monocle, Aeon, and TIME Magazine.

"[Balaska] illuminates not only the distinctive nature of philosophy, but its ineliminable role in the perennial human task of making sense of ourselves and our place in the universe.” — Stephen Mulhall

events.title: The Self, The Soul, and the Nature of Reality

profiles.name: Maria Balaska
profiles.tagline: Philosopher Mapping the Edges of Human Experience

profiles.bio:
"I think it's ridiculous to dismiss philosophy because you are a proponent of science."

Jack Symes is a public philosopher, writer, and researcher at Durham University. He is best known as the host of The Panpsycast Philosophy Podcast, one of the UK's most popular higher education podcasts. Jack regularly appears on major public platforms, such as BBC Radio 4. In 2026, he was the featured participant in the Jubilee debate programme Surrounded, appearing in the episode "1 Vegan vs 20 Meat Eaters."

Jack also hosts live shows, including An Evening With theatre events and panels at The Royal Institution.He is the author of four books, including Philosophers on God: Talking about Existence and Defeating the Evil-God Challenge: In Defence of God’s Goodness. Jack was awarded the BBC New Generation Thinker Prize in 2024.

"Jack Symes guides us charmingly and authoritatively, with a wit and freshness that enlivens without trivializing." — Stephen Fry
profiles.name: Jack Symes
profiles.tagline: Philosopher and BBC New Generation Thinker

profiles.bio:
"If we don’t fix climate change, all the development advances that we have achieved will go backwards again."

Janos Pasztor is a leading figure in international climate governance, with close to five decades of experience in energy, environment, and climate change policy. He retired in 2023 after a career spent shaping global responses to climate change, including the governance of emerging technologies such as carbon dioxide removal and solar radiation modification.
From 2016 to 2023, he was Senior Fellow at the Carnegie Council for Ethics in International Affairs and Executive Director of the Carnegie Climate Governance Initiative (C2G). Earlier, he served as UN Assistant Secretary-General for Climate Change and Senior Advisor to Secretary-General Ban Ki-moon, and held senior roles at WWF-International. His UN career also included leading the Secretary-General's Climate Change Support Team, serving as Executive Secretary of the High-level Panel on Global Sustainability, and working for many years at the UNFCCC Secretariat.

"[I have] deep gratitude for Mr. Pasztor’s dedicated service and leadership" — Ban Ki-moon
profiles.name: Janos Pasztor
profiles.tagline: Diplomat at the centre of climate policy

profiles.bio:
"The beauty of administrative data is that every interaction between a person and a public service is captured.”

Emma Gordon is one of Britain's leading figures in the world of administrative data research, working at the intersection of government, academia, and public policy. As Director of the ADR UK Strategic Hub and Director of ADR England, she oversees a £105 million programme opening up access to government data to support research and inform policy decisions.

Gordon is also Editor-in-Chief of the International Journal of Population Data Science, and began her career as a post-doctoral researcher on the Avon Longitudinal Study of Parents and Children.
profiles.name: Emma Gordon
profiles.tagline: Researcher Unlocking Government Data for Public Good

profiles.bio: Miriam Cohen has been teaching philosophy to graduates and undergraduates since 1994, from lecture halls at UCL, Oxford and Heythrop to classrooms at Camden Girls School, where she currently teaches A Level philosophy. With a BA and MPhil from UCL, her intellectual home is in political philosophy and Plato: the big questions of power, justice and how we ought to live together.
profiles.name: Miriam Cohen
profiles.tagline: Teacher at The Philosophy Foundation

profiles.name: Matilda Atkins
profiles.tagline: Prominent philosophy educator

profiles.bio: Zoe Drewitt is a Specialist Philosophy Teacher and mentor for The Philosophy Foundation. She studied philosophy at the University London and continues to facilitate philosophical enquiries for all forms - from six to ninety-six.
profiles.name: Zoe Drewitt
profiles.tagline: Philosophy specialist facilitating debate for all ages

acts.bio: Glastonbury (BBC Introducing), Latitude, and Great Escape veterans. This London indie-pop duo is capturing the UK music scene with cinematic songwriting and tight harmonies. A premier festival draw, they have earned coveted main support slots on major UK tours alongside indie titans Wet Leg and The Big Moon.
acts.name: Prima Queen

acts.bio: Glastonbury and WOMEX favourites whose exhilarating sound blends Arabic, Balkan, Turkish, and Mediterranean traditions with psychedelic folk and driving electric rhythms. This international collective has performed across Europe, North America, the Middle East, and Asia, collaborating with Africa Express and delivering joyous, high-energy performances that unite audiences through music.
acts.name: The Turbans

acts.bio: First LGBT artist awarded the Burke Medal for Outstanding Contribution to the Arts. Fusing electronics, viola, and piano, his sold-out Scala and Shepherd's Bush shows ignited a major-label bidding war. A visionary creator, he has collaborated with Tilda Swinton and toured the world playing viola for Patti Smith.
acts.name: Patrick Wolf

acts.bio: Glastonbury and Royal Albert Hall veteran with BBC Introducing backing. Transitioning from a celebrated jazz vocalist to an alt-folk-rock powerhouse, Hopkins’s debut EP Animal earned raves for its blues-soaked grit. Praised by BBC Introducing for her powerful vocals, she brings an impassioned, commanding live presence to any stage.
acts.name: Elly Hopkins

acts.bio: Ben Cipolla is a Bristol-based singer-songwriter known for his rich, velvety vocals versatile guitar playing and captivating live performances. Blending influences from Nick Drake and Jack Johnson with his own unique style, he creates intimate, memorable songs. Recently his England football anthems have reached over 15 million views, while his Clare Teal collaboration Love and Affection surpassed 30,000 streams.
acts.name: Ben Cipolla

acts.bio: Green Man Festival alumni with major NME acclaim. Fronted by exceptional singer-songwriter Eve Appleton-Scott, this rising alt-folk powerhouse has captured the industry's attention with their striking debut album Bible Black. Combining intricate storytelling with rich, multi-instrumental arrangements, they are a captivating new force on the UK scene.
acts.name: Eve Appleton Band

acts.bio: Ava Hincks is a singer songwriter from London who found her sound in Bristol performing in sold out gigs and has recently achieved an MA in musical theatre at LAMDA. Ava grew up listening to the Beatles and blondie and uses those as inspiration in her music! Ava has been played on BBC Introducing and one of her proudest moments was hearing her song “drought” in the sold out fringe show fruit cake!
acts.name: Ava Hincks

acts.bio: London-based indie folk-pop harmony trio formed in 2020. They blend the rawness and melancholy of 90s alternative folk (reminiscent of Elliott Smith or Bright Eyes) with the melodic warmth and playfulness of late-60s pop.
acts.name: Preen

acts.bio:
Miranda Joy is a London-based singer-songwriter whose soulful voice, heartfelt songwriting and captivating live performances have earned her a growing reputation on the UK's independent music scene. Blending elements of soul, pop and contemporary singer-songwriter influences, she crafts songs that are both emotionally honest and effortlessly memorable, connecting with audiences through powerful storytelling and rich melodies.
Performing since her teens, Miranda has appeared at an impressive range of venues, festivals and showcase events, including The Great Escape Festival, Rye International Jazz & Blues Festival, O2 Academy Islington, Green Note, Crazy Coqs and Camden Assembly. Her music has also reached audiences beyond the stage, with her song The Fall featured on the BBC One Super Bowl Highlights programme and her songwriting showcased across television and radio worldwide.
Alongside her solo releases, Miranda is a sought-after collaborator, co-writing with emerging artists and lending her distinctive vocals to a variety of projects. Recent singles, including Wasting My Time, have received support from BBC Introducing, further cementing her status as an artist to watch. Whether performing intimate acoustic sets or fronting her all-female band, Miranda Joy delivers an engaging, authentic live experience that leaves a lasting impression.
acts.name: Miranda Joy

acts.bio: Rising UK alternative talent with thousands of digital streams. Known for her evocative, genre-fluid songwriting that spans indie-pop, neo-soul, and electro-pop, Katie Alice is a staple of the underground touring circuit. Her captivating live performances and intimate lyrical delivery consistently draw loyal crowds across major independent music venues.
acts.name: Katie Alice

acts.bio: Captivating modern multi-instrumentalist and classical-crossover talent. Carrying a legacy of rich musical heritage, Grace Harvey bridges the gap between traditional musicianship and contemporary live appeal. Her elegant arrangements and virtuosic execution make her a highly sophisticated, atmospheric addition to acoustic, classical, and independent festival line ups alike.
acts.name: Grace Harvey

acts.bio:
Good Weather for an Airstrike is an ambient music project that was initially conceived at the beginning of 2009 by Winchester, UK-based Tom Honey. GWFAA’s music has been streamed over 75 million times across the major streaming platforms, as well as being featured regularly on BBC Introducing, KEXP and Channel 4.

They are a featured artist on the sleep, meditation and relaxation app ‘Calm’ (Apple’s App of the year + Google Play Editors Choice) and has been featured on New York Magazine and Nowness. Their work draws on all of his musical influences and presents itself as a rich tapestry of lulling drone  that hints at a diluted form of post-rock.
Now as a four-piece for live performances, they have played sold out shows alongside Flyte, Plaid & Nordic Giants across the UK.
acts.name: Good weather for an airstrike

acts.bio: Recently reviewed in the Financial Times, Sue Harding is getting noticed! This West Country-based singer, songwriter & guitar player's unique vocal-range & heartfelt delivery creates a hauntingly beautiful sound with a retro sensibility, referencing the song-writing of the 1960s & '70s.
acts.name: Sue Harding

acts.bio: Viral acoustic-folk artist with over 17K TikTok followers. This 23-year-old singer-songwriter delivers upbeat, heart-on-sleeve acoustic folk inspired by Sam Fender and Johnny Flynn. Having gigged heavily across the UK and Ireland, his rapidly growing digital fan base translates into packed venues and an undeniable, intimate crowd connection.
acts.name: Ned Holland

acts.bio: Purbeck Rising winners and UK folk festival circuit favourites. This London-based contemporary folk duo blends intricate multi-instrumental songwriting with classically trained vocals and traditional whistle. Famed for their ethereal, full-band arrangements, they regularly command packed crowds at acoustic stages and independent festivals across the United Kingdom.
acts.name: Delphis

acts.bio:
A storyteller first and foremost, Tia Meraki is a singer-songwriter and poet based on the North Devon coast. Combining her love of words & melody to weave tales ranging from the personal through to the mythological, she's been busy writing and performing while carving out a unique sound with its roots in the folk tradition.
"Tia delivers very cleverly written and compellingly poetic songs with a unique and softly powerful vocal." - Graeme Moncrieff, Dusk Brothers
acts.name: Tia Meraki

acts.bio:
As seen on Amazon's Last One Laughing, Dave’s Hypothetical, ITV’s Hey Tracey, Comedy Central’s Roast Battle, and as a recurring guest on 8 out of 10 Cats Does Countdown and 8 Out of 10 Cats, Harriet Kemsley is a tour de force of the comedy world. She has starred in the Viceland reality sitcom Bobby and Harriet: Get Married, which she co-created and co-wrote with her husband Bobby Mair, to huge critical acclaim. Her other credits include hosting the BBC Radio 4 Comedy Club, The Radio 1 Comedy Lounge, BBC3’s Comedy Marathon, The One Show and Kevin Hart’s LOL Live. Harriet’s awards include the Leicester Mercury New Act of the Year Finalist, Funny’s Funny Winner, Up The Creek New Act of the Year Winner, and Leicester Square New Act of the Year Finalist. Known for her sharp, autobiographical style that pairs an optimistically ditzy stage persona with surprisingly dark subjects, she has been described by Time Out as ‘a very funny rising star’ and as one of Rhod Gilbert’s ‘Ten Comics to See’ in the Mail on Sunday.

"Reckless good fun. ★★★★" - The Guardian.
acts.name: Harriet Kemsley

acts.bio:
Funny Women finalist, part of the BBC Comedy Asian Network and listed in Dua Lipa’s ‘Service 95’ magazine as one of “5 new faces to know bringing a fresh perspective to the comedy scene”, Fatiya Saleh is hot off performances at Latitude Festival. She has since featured in the Comedy Queen’s sold‑out UK tour. Born and raised in North West London to a Somali mother and Yemeni father, Fathiya’s comedy offers her own cutting perspectives on topics exploring cultural identity and family dynamics, the absurdities of everyday workplace life and challenges, what it is like being one of the “girlies” and navigating the world as a young Muslim. It's tough out there, but at least it's funny content. Sometimes. 

"An absolute delight." - Chortle
acts.name: Fathiya Saleh

acts.bio:
His clips have racked up over 100 million views online, and he has provided tour support for Stephen Bailey, Reuben Solo and Max Fosh. His split-bill Edinburgh Fringe show, Cold Brew Comedy, sold out across all four weekends of the festival. Alfie Dundas is known for his smart, self-deprecating and on-the-line comedy that blends personal confession with sharp cultural observation. He regularly performs at top comedy clubs across the UK, including The Comedy Store, Top Secret Comedy Club & The Frog and Bucket. 

"Shows a lot of promise... I wouldn't be surprised if he goes far. ★★★★" - EdFringe Review
acts.name: Alfie Dundas

acts.bio:
Ever served so hard you almost toppled a government? After gaining attention for her short film GUTS, Maia Tassalini began performing stand-up in 2024 and later that year reached the final of the BBC New Comedian of the Year Award.  She is a member of the Pleasance Comedy Reserve 2025, a Soho Comedy Labs Plus alumna, and made her full Edinburgh Fringe debut this year. Her hyper-articulate, theatrical stand-up has rapidly marked her out as one of the UK’s most exciting new cult comic voices. Tassalini channels the muse (Monica Lewinsky) to boldly ask the question on everyone's lips: is there anything more cursed than being 22 and stunning?

"Maia is a natural. Born to do it. Unreal!" - Shaparak Khorsandi
acts.name: Maia Tassalini

acts.bio:
Lewis Garnham is a star comedian on the rise — "a gifted and spirited storyteller," raves Chortle (★★★★). His 2025 Australian tour sold out six cities outright, and his 22-night Melbourne International Comedy Festival run sold so fast he added 10 more shows — which also sold out instantly. The Scotsman (★★★★) calls him "a very natural, assured raconteur," while ArtsHub (★★★★) praises his "humorous connections and meaningful punchlines." His special Stream of Contentedness drops ahead of his 2026 tour.

"Good. So good. Faultless." - Fringe World
acts.name: Lewis Garnham

acts.bio:
BBC New Comedy Award and Channel 4's Sean Lock Awards finalist Marty Gleeson is an Irish comedian making waves in the UK.

Renowned for her offbeat, captivating, and whimsical performance style, Gleeson was crowned LGBTQ+ New Comedian of the Year 2024 and was also chosen to be a part of the prestigious Pleasance Comedy Reserve at the Edinburgh Fringe 2024.

With over 30 million views online and tour support for Vittorio Angelone under her belt, Gleeson is a comic making big juicy turbulent waves, run for cover. No one is safe.
acts.name: Marty Gleeson

acts.bio:
Chantel Nash started performing stand-up comedy half way through 2022, and her effortless charm has been winning over audiences one postcode at a time. Only a year later in 2023, Chantel reached the finals of prestigious competitions So You Think You’re Funny? and the BBC New Comedy Awards, which was aired on BBC One.
Since then, Chantel has appeared on the hugely popular podcast Parenting Hell with Josh Widdicombe and Rob Beckett, Comedy Central Live, and Mo Gilligan’s Spotlight on Audible.
She has also shared the stage with some of the biggest names in UK Comedy, including Romesh Ranganathan, Kerry Godliman, Mo Gilligan, and Judi Love, and supported Russell Kane and Josh Widdicombe on their most recent tours.
This fast rising future star of comedy is one you will certainly want to see.
acts.name: Chantel Nash

acts.bio:
Jen Nolan burst onto the comedy scene in 2022, banging down the door with a top-knot on her head and a cheeky smile on her face. With sharp wit and unfiltered cockney charm, she delivers hilarious and heartfelt stories from her life growing up in East London, all with a bold attitude and relatable warmth that wins over audiences night after night.
Jen was hand-picked to perform in the highly acclaimed Comedy Reserve Show for Pleasance Theatres, and will be performing every night at the Edinburgh Festival this August. When she’s not lighting up the stage, Jen co-hosts the Pokes & Jokes podcast with Grace Neutral, where comedy and candid conversation collide.
Best in Class 2023, Leicester Square Theatre New Comedian of the Year semi finalist 2023, Queerovision Champion of Champions, LGBT New Comedian of the Year semi-finalist, Leicester Comedy Festival Circuit Breakers 2025.
acts.name: Jen Nolan

acts.bio:
Cult cabaret royalty Bourgeois & Maurice (real names Liv Morris and George Heyworth) have spent almost two decades at the top of London's neo-cabaret scene. Since forming in 2007, the duo have staged multiple full-length theatre shows, released four studio albums, and won Best Music-Based Act at the London Cabaret Awards. Their 2016 Fringe show ranked among the top 20 best-reviewed comedy shows at Edinburgh that year, and they've twice taken Time Out's Alternative Eurovision title. Bourgeois & Maurice's work explores sex, politics, hedonism and the general absurdity of being alive, all wrapped in sequins and a very good key change. 

★★★★★ The Scotsman (Pleasure Seekers, Soho Theatre)

★★★★ "Modern day Music Hall stars" — The Guardian
★★★★ Independent
acts.name: Bourgeois & Maurice

acts.bio:
Festival favourites Alex Farrow and Chelsea Birkby return to HowTheLightGetsIn to wow audiences with their hilarious big-thinking comedy. Of course they are festival favourites, given that the world's largest philosophy and music festival naturally gravitates towards comedians who happen to be former philosophy teachers and philosophy graduates. Alex Farrow races through WW3, medical trials, technology and Freudian father figures at punchline-dense speed. Mock the Week writer Chelsea Birkby playfully combines pop culture and philosophy, unpacking being in the moment and desire.

"An intelligent new star with a skill for strong joke writing." - Comedy.co.uk
"Sharp mind behind the sweet exterior." - **** Telegraph
acts.name: Alex Farrow & Chelsea Birkby
